  3102                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  3103                                  
  3104                                  ;============================================================================
  3105                                  ; MSHEAD.ASM (MSDOS 6.0, 1991)
  3106                                  ;============================================================================
  3107                                  ; 16/07/2018 - Retro DOS 3.0
  3108                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3109                                  ; 24/04/2019 - Retro DOS 4.0
  3110                                  
  3111                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
  3112                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3113                                  ; FILE : ORIGIN.INC
  3114                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3115                                  ; This is included in origin.asm and mshead.asm. Contains the equate that
  3116                                  ; is used for ORGing the DOS code.
  3117                                  ;
  3118                                  ; Brief Description of the necessacity of this ORG:
  3119                                  ; -------------------------------------------------
  3120                                  ;
  3121                                  ; A special problem exits when running out of the HMA. The HMA starts at 
  3122                                  ; address FFFF:10. There is no place in the HMA with an offset of zero.
  3123                                  ; This means programs running out off the HMA must use non-zero offset base
  3124                                  ; addresses. It also means that if we're running multiple programs from the
  3125                                  ; HMA, the base offset of each segment must atleast be as big as all of the
  3126                                  ; HMA segments that precede it.
  3127                                  ; 
  3128                                  ; One solution to this problem to ORG each module at 64K minus its size.
  3129                                  ; For instance a code segment 1234h bytes in length would org'd at edcbh.
  3130                                  ; This gives max. flexibility regarding it's location in the HMA. By 
  3131                                  ; selecting segment values between f124h and ffffh it could be located 
  3132                                  ; anywhere in the HMA. The problem with this is that programs with such 
  3133                                  ; high ORGs would not be able to run in low RAM.
  3134                                  ;
  3135                                  ; A compromise solution is to set the ORG address somewhere between 0010h
  3136                                  ; and ffffh - their size. In the particular case of the BIOS and the DOS 
  3137                                  ; the following solution has been implemented:
  3138                                  ;
  3139                                  ; The Bios Code segment will have a very small offset and run at the very
  3140                                  ; front of the HMA, after the VDISK header. THE Dos Code segment will have 
  3141                                  ; a base offset of (700+<min. size off RAM based BIOS>+<min. size of the DOS
  3142                                  ; DATA segment when DOS is running low>). This will reflect the lowest 
  3143                                  ; possible physical address at which DOS code will run, while still providing
  3144                                  ; max. possible flexibility in HMA positioning. This offset MUST NOT be 
  3145                                  ; smaller then that 20+size of Bios Code segment when running high. This is 
  3146                                  ; mostly true.
  3147                                  ;
  3148                                  ; Also this ORG'd value must be communicated to the BIOS. This is done by
  3149                                  ; putting this value after the first jmp instruction in the DOS code in
  3150                                  ; mshead.asm. 
  3151                                  ;
  3152                                  ; In order for the stripz utility to know how many zeroes to be stripped 
  3153                                  ; out, this value is placed at the beginning of the binary in origin.asm.
  3154                                  ;
  3155                                  ; Revision History:
  3156                                  ;
  3157                                  ; Currently this is being done manually. Therefore any change in the DOS DATA
  3158                                  ; Size or the BIOS size should be reflected here. --- Feb 90
  3159                                  ;
  3160                                  ; BDSIZE.INC contains the equates for BIODATASIZE, BIOCODESIZ and DOSDATASIZ.
  3161                                  ; A utility called getsize will obtain the corresponding values from msdos
  3162                                  ; and msbio.map and update the values in BDSIZ.INC if they are different. 
  3163                                  ; DOS should now be built using the batch file makedos.bat which invokes this
  3164                                  ; utility. The FORMAT of BDSIZE.INC should not be changed as getsize is 
  3165                                  ; dependant on that.				  --- Apr 3 '90
  3166                                  ;
  3167                                  ; For ROMDOS, however, there is no need to org the doscode to any location
  3168                                  ; other than zero.  Therefore the stripz utility will not need to be used,
  3169                                  ; so the offset will not need to be included at the beginning of the code
  3170                                  ; segment.  Also, the BIOS can just assume that the resident code begins
  3171                                  ; at offset zero within the segment.
  3172                                  ; 
  3173                                  ;
  3174                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3175                                  
  3176                                  BIODATASTART	EQU	00700h
  3177                                  ;include	bdsize.inc	; this sets the values:
  3178                                  				;	BIODATASIZ
  3179                                  				;	BIOCODESIZ
  3180                                  				;	DOSDATASIZ
  3181                                  
  3182                                  ; 05/12/2022
  3183                                  ;BIODATASIZ EQU 00910H	; 0900h for MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS
  3184                                  			; 0900h for MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS
  3185                                  ;BIOCODESIZ EQU 01A70H	; 1A70h for MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS
  3186                                  			; 1A60h for MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS
  3187                                  ;DOSDATASIZ EQU 01370H	; 1370h for MSDOS 6.21 IO.SYS
  3188                                  			; 1370h for MSDOS 5.0 IO.SYS
  3189                                  ;ifndef ROMDOS
  3190                                  ;
  3191                                  ;BYTSTART	EQU    	BIODATASTART+BIODATASIZ+BIOCODESIZ+DOSDATASIZ
  3192                                  ;PARASTART	EQU	(BYTSTART + 0FH) AND (NOT 0FH)	
  3193                                  ;
  3194                                  ;else
  3195                                  ;
  3196                                  ;BYTSTART	EQU	0
  3197                                  ;PARASTART	EQU	0
  3198                                  ;
  3199                                  ;endif ; ROMDOS

  3304                                  ;;hkn YRTAB & MONTAB moved to DOSDATA in ms_data.asm
  3305                                  ;	I_am	YRTAB,8,<200,166,200,165,200,165,200,165>   ; [SYSTEM]
  3306                                  ;	I_am	MONTAB,12,<31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31> ; [SYSTEM]

  3309                                  ; YRTAB & MONTAB moved from TABLE segment in ms_table.asm
  3310                                  ;
  3311                                  ;	I_am    YRTAB,8,<200,166,200,165,200,165,200,165>   
  3312                                  ;	I_am    MONTAB,12,<31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31> 
  3313                                  
  3314                                  ; This is the error code mapping table for INT 21 errors. This table defines
  3315                                  ; those error codes which are "allowed" for each system call. If the error
  3316                                  ; code ABOUT to be returned is not "allowed" for the call, the correct action
  3317                                  ; is to return the "real" error via Extended error, and one of the allowed
  3318                                  ; errors on the actual call.
  3319                                  ;
  3320                                  ; The table is organized as follows:
  3321                                  ;
  3322                                  ;    Each entry in the table is of variable size, but the first
  3323                                  ;       two bytes are always:
  3324                                  ;
  3325                                  ;       Call#,Cnt of bytes following this byte
  3326                                  ;
  3327                                  ; EXAMPLE:
  3328                                  ;       Call 61 (OPEN)
  3329                                  ;
  3330                                  ;       DB      61,5,12,3,2,4,5
  3331                                  ;
  3332                                  ;       61 is the AH INT 21 call value for OPEN.
  3333                                  ;        5 indicates that there are 5 bytes after this byte (12,3,2,4,5).
  3334                                  ;       Next five bytes are those error codes which are "allowed" on OPEN.
  3335                                  ;       The order of these values is not important EXCEPT FOR THE LAST ONE (in
  3336                                  ;       this case 5).  The last value will be the one returned on the call if
  3337                                  ;       the "real" error is not one of the allowed ones.
  3338                                  ;
  3339                                  ; There are a number of calls (for instance all of the FCB calls) for which
  3340                                  ;   there is NO entry.  This means that NO error codes are returned on this
  3341                                  ;   call, so set up an Extended error and leave the current error code alone.
  3342                                  ;
  3343                                  ; The table is terminated by a call value of 0FFh
  3344                                  
  3345                                  ;PUBLIC I21_MAP_E_TAB
  3346                                  	; 10/08/2018
  3347                                  
  3348                                  ; 29/04/2019
  3349                                  ; DOSCODE:3DE9h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  3350                                  ; 04/11/2022
  3351                                  ; DOSCODE:3DDBh	(MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  3352                                  ; 01/01/2024
  3353                                  ; DOSCODE:3F1Bh	(PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)

  4128                                  
  4129                                  ; DOSCODE:40CCh (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  4130                                  
  4131                                  ; ==========================================================================
  4132                                  ;
  4133                                  ; The Quit entry point is where all INT 20h's come from. These are old- style
  4134                                  ; exit system calls. The CS of the caller indicates which Process is dying.
  4135                                  ; The error code is presumed to be 0. We simulate an ABORT system call.
  4136                                  ;
  4137                                  ; ==========================================================================
  4138                                  
  4139                                  SYSTEM_CALL:    ; PROC NEAR
  4140                                  
  4141                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4142                                  ; DOSCODE:40BFh (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
  4143                                  
  4144                                  ;entry	QUIT				
  4145                                  QUIT:				; INT 20H entry point
  4146                                  	;MOV	AH,0
  4147 000002D9 30E4                    	xor	ah,ah ; 08/07/2018
  4148 000002DB EB36                    	JMP     SHORT SAVREGS
  4149                                  
  4150                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4151                                  
  4152                                  	; The system call in AH is out of the range that we know how
  4153                                  	; to handle. We arbitrarily set the contents of AL to 0 and
  4154                                  	; IRET. Note that we CANNOT set the carry flag to indicate an
  4155                                  	; error as this may break some programs compatability.
  4156                                  
  4157                                  BADCALL:
  4158                                          ;MOV	AL,0
  4159 000002DD 30C0                    	xor	al,al ; 08/07/2018
  4160                                  IRETT:	; 06/05/2019
  4161                                  _IRET:
  4162 000002DF CF                              IRET
  4163                                  
  4164                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4165                                  
  4166                                  ; 01/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  4167                                  ; DOSCODE:40D3h (MSDOS 6.21 MSDOS.SYS)
  4168                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4169                                  ; DOSCODE:40C6h (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4170                                  
  4171                                  	; An alternative method of entering the system is to perform a
  4172                                  	; CALL 5 in the program segment prefix with the contents of CL
  4173                                  	; indicating what system call the user would like. A subset of
  4174                                  	; the possible system calls is allowed here only the
  4175                                  	; CPM-compatible calls may get dispatched.
  4176                                  
  4177                                  		; System call entry point and dispatcher
  4178                                  CALL_ENTRY:
  4179 000002E0 1E                      	push	DS
  4180                                  	;getdseg <DS>			; DS -> DosData, ASSUME DS:DosSeg
  4181 000002E1 2E8E1E[0700]            	mov	ds,[cs:DosDSeg]
  4182 000002E6 8F06[EC05]              	pop	word [SAVEDS]		; Save original DS
  4183                                  
  4184 000002EA 58                              POP     AX                      ; IP from the long call at 5
  4185 000002EB 58                              POP     AX                      ; Segment from the long call at 5
  4186 000002EC 8F06[8405]              	POP	WORD [USER_SP]		; IP from the CALL 5
  4187                                  
  4188                                  		; Re-order the stack to simulate an interrupt 21.
  4189                                  
  4190 000002F0 9C                      	PUSHF				; Start re-ordering the stack
  4191 000002F1 FA                      	CLI
  4192 000002F2 50                              PUSH    AX                      ; Save segment
  4193 000002F3 FF36[8405]                      PUSH	WORD [USER_SP]		; Stack now ordered as if INT had been used
  4194                                  	; 04/11/2022
  4195                                  	; DOSCODE:40EAh (MSDOS 6.21 MSDOS.SYS)
  4196                                  	; DOSCODE:40DDh (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  4197 000002F7 FF36[EC05]              	push	word [SAVEDS]
  4198 000002FB 1F                      	pop	ds
  4199                                  	;
  4200                                  	;cmp	cl,36
  4201 000002FC 80F924                          CMP     CL,MAXCALL              ; This entry point doesn't get as many calls
  4202 000002FF 77DC                            JA      SHORT BADCALL
  4203 00000301 88CC                            MOV     AH,CL
  4204                                  	; 08/07/2018
  4205 00000303 EB0E                    	jmp	short SAVREGS
  4206                                  
  4207                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4208                                  
  4209                                  ; 01/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  4210                                  ; 01/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0

  4975                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4976                                  ;
  4977                                  ; Procedure Name : ABSDRD
  4978                                  ;
  4979                                  ; Interrupt 25 handler. Performs absolute disk read.
  4980                                  ; Inputs:	AL - 0-based drive number
  4981                                  ;		DS:BX point to destination buffer
  4982                                  ;		CX number of logical sectors to read
  4983                                  ;		DX starting logical sector number (0-based)
  4984                                  ; Outputs:	Original flags still on stack
  4985                                  ;		Carry set
  4986                                  ;		    AH error from BIOS
  4987                                  ;		    AL same as low byte of DI from INT 24
  4988                                  ;
  4989                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  4990                                          ;procedure   ABSDRD,FAR
  4991                                  ABSDRD:
  4992                                  	; 15/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  4993                                  	; MSDOS 6.21 (DOSCODE:42E5h)
  4994                                  	; 04/11/2022
  4995                                  	; MSDOS 5.0 (DOSCODE:42D8h)
  4996                                  
  4997                                  	; 02/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
  4998                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:43C4h
  4999                                  	
  5000                                  	;;;
  5001 00000541 30E4                    	xor     ah,ah	; ah=0		; Interrupt 25h handler (ah=0)
  5002 00000543 31F6                    	xor     si,si	; si=0		; clear read/write mode flags
  5003                                  					; (used with INT 21h ax=7305h)
  5004                                  FAT32_ABSDRD:	; ah=1 si=0 cf=0 (jump from '_$FAT32EXT')
  5005                                  	; 25/06/2024
  5006                                  	;cli ; *
  5007                                  	;clc ; not necessary
  5008                                  				; INT 21h
  5009                                  				;	AX = 7305h
  5010                                  				; FAT32 - EXTENDED ABSOLUTE DISK READ/WRITE
  5011                                  				;	CX = FFFFh
  5012                                  				;	DL = drive number (01h=A:, etc.)
  5013                                  				;	SI = read/write mode flags
  5014                                  				;	DS:BX -> disk I/O packet
  5015                                  				;
  5016                                  				; Extended Absolute Disk Read/Write mode flags:
  5017                                  				;
  5018                                  				;	Bit(s)  Description
  5019                                  				;	0	direction (0=read, 1=write)
  5020                                  				;	12-1	reserved (0)
  5021                                  				;	14-13	write type (should be 00 on reads).
  5022                                  				;		00 unknown data.
  5023                                  				;		01 FAT data.
  5024                                  				;		10 directory data.
  5025                                  				;		11 file data
  5026                                  				;	15     reserved (0)
  5027                                  				;
  5028                                  				; Format of disk read/write packet:
  5029                                  				;
  5030                                  				;	Offset Size    Description
  5031                                  				;	00h    DWORD   sector number
  5032                                  				;	04h    WORD    number of sectors to r/w
  5033                                  				;	06h    DWORD   transfer address
  5034                                  				;
  5035                                  				; ref: Ralf Brown's Interrupt List
  5036                                  	;;;
  5037                                  absdrd_1:
  5038                                  	; MSDOS 6.0

  5049 00000551 58                      	pop	ax			; restore AX value
  5050

  5052                                  	; We shall save es on the user stack here. We need to use ES in
  5053                                  	; order to access the DOSDATA variables AbsRdWr_SS/SP at exit
  5054                                  	; time in order to restore the user stack.
  5055                                  
  5056 00000552 06                      	push	es  ; ****		; M072
  5057                                  
  5058                                  	; 25/06/2024

  5075

  5077                                  ;
  5078                                  ; NOTE! Due to an obscure bug in the 80286, you cannot use the ROMDOS
  5079                                  ; version of the getdseg macro with the SS register! An interrupt will
  5080                                  ; sneak through.
  5081

  5084

  5086

  5088                                  ;	mov	ds, cs:[BioDataSeg]
  5089                                  ;	assume	ds:bdata
  5090                                  ;
  5091                                  ;	mov	ss, ds:[DosDataSg]
  5092                                  ;	assume	ss:DOSDATA
  5093                                  ;
  5094                                  ;endif ; ROMDOS
  5095                                  					; 02/01/2024
  5096 0000056B BC[2009]                	MOV	SP,DSKSTACK	 	;"@#IBM:12.01.2003.build_1.32#@ IBMDOS.COM(USA)"
  5097                                  					; (PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)

  5115                                  
  5116                                  	; Here is a gross temporary fix to get around a serious design flaw in
  5117                                  	;  the secondary cache. The secondary cache does not check for media
  5118                                  	;  changed (it should). Hence, you can change disks, do an absolute
  5119                                  	;  read, and get data from the previous disk. To get around this,
  5120                                  	;  we just won't use the secondary cache for absolute disk reads.
  5121                                  	;                                                      -mw 8/5/88

  5224                                  ; Procedure Name : ABSDWRT
  5225                                  ;
  5226                                  ; Interrupt 26 handler. Performs absolute disk write.
  5227                                  ; Inputs:	AL - 0-based drive number

  5251                                  FAT32_ABSDWRT:	; ah=1 si=1 cf=0 (jump from '_$FAT32EXT')
  5252                                  
  5253                                  				; INT 21h
  5254                                  				;	AX = 7305h
  5255                                  				; FAT32 - EXTENDED ABSOLUTE DISK READ/WRITE
  5256                                  				;	CX = FFFFh

  5258                                  				;	SI = read/write mode flags
  5259                                  				;	DS:BX -> disk I/O packet
  5260                                  				;
  5261                                  				; Extended Absolute Disk Read/Write mode flags:
  5262                                  				;
  5263                                  				;	Bit(s)  Description
  5264                                  				;	0	direction (0=read, 1=write)
  5265                                  				;	12-1	reserved (0)
  5266                                  				;	14-13	write type (should be 00 on reads).
  5267                                  				;		00 unknown data.
  5268                                  				;		01 FAT data.
  5269                                  				;		10 directory data.
  5270                                  				;		11 file data
  5271                                  				;	15     reserved (0)
  5272                                  				;
  5273                                  				; Format of disk read/write packet:
  5274                                  				;
  5275                                  				;	Offset Size    Description
  5276                                  				;	00h    DWORD   sector number
  5277                                  				;	04h    WORD    number of sectors to r/w
  5278                                  				;	06h    DWORD   transfer address

  6491                                  ;M044; Start of changes
  6492                                  ; Winoldap has a bug in that its calculations for the Windows memory image
  6493                                  ; to save is off by 1 para. This para can happen to be a Windows arena if the
  6494                                  ; DOS top of memory happens to be at an odd boundary (as is the case when
  6495                                  ; UMBs are present). This is because Windows builds its arenas only at even
  6496                                  ; para boundaries. This arena now gets trashed when Windows is swapped back
  6497                                  ; in leading to a crash. Winoldap issues callouts when it swaps Windows out
  6498                                  ; and back in. We sit on these callouts. On the Windows swapout, we save the
  6499                                  ; last para of the Windows memory block and then restore this para on the
  6500                                  ; Windows swapin callout. 
  6501

  6863                                  ; DOSMES.ASM (MSDOS 2.11, 1983)

  6865                                  ; OEMFunction key is expected to process a single function
  6866                                  ;   key input from a device and dispatch to the proper
  6867                                  ;   routines leaving all registers UNTOUCHED.
  6868                                  ;
  6869                                  ; Inputs:   CS, SS are DOSGROUP
  6870                                  ; Outputs:  None. This function is expected to JMP to onw of
  6871                                  ;           the following labels:
  6872                                  ;
  6873                                  ;           GetCh       - ignore the sequence
  6874                                  ;           TwoEsc      - insert an ESCChar in the buffer
  6875                                  ;           ExitIns     - toggle insert mode
  6876                                  ;           EnterIns    - toggle insert mode
  6877                                  ;           BackSp      - move backwards one space
  6878                                  ;           ReEdit      - reedit the line with a new template
  6879                                  ;           KilNew      - discard the current line and start from scratch
  6880                                  ;           CopyLin     - copy the rest of the template into the line
  6881                                  ;           SkipStr     - read the next character and skip to it in the template
  6882                                  ;           CopyStr     - read next char and copy from template to line until char
  6883                                  ;           SkipOne     - advance position in template one character
  6884                                  ;           CopyOne     - copy next character in template into line
  6885                                  ;           CtrlZ       - place a ^Z into the template
  6886                                  ; Registers that are allowed to be modified by this function are:
  6887                                  ;           AX, CX, BP
  6888                                  
  6889                                  ; 13/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  6890                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6891                                  ; DOSCODE:4820h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  6892                                  
  6893                                  ; 05/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  6894                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6895                                  ; DOSCODE:4813h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)

  6900                                  
  6901                                  OEMFunctionKey:
  6902 00000A92 E8450E                  	CALL	_$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO	; Get the second byte of the sequence
  6903 00000A95 B10E                    	MOV     CL,ESCTABLEN ; 14	; length of table for scan
  6904 00000A97 57                      	PUSH    DI                      ; save DI (cannot change it!)
  6905 00000A98 BF[680A]                	MOV     DI,ESCTAB		; offset of second byte table
  6906 00000A9B 06                      	push	es
  6907 00000A9C 0E                      	push	cs
  6908 00000A9D 07                      	pop	es
  6909 00000A9E F2AE                    	REPNE   SCASB                   ; Look it up in the table

  7530                                  ;BREAK <$International - return country-dependent information>
  7531                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  7532                                  ;
  7533                                  ; Procedure Name : $INTERNATIONAL
  7534                                  ;
  7535                                  ; Inputs:
  7536                                  ;	MOV	AH,International
  7537                                  ;	MOV	AL,country	(al = 0 => current country)
  7538                                  ;      [MOV	BX,country]
  7539                                  ;	LDS	DX,block
  7540                                  ;	INT	21
  7541                                  ; Function:
  7542                                  ;	give users an idea of what country the application is running
  7543                                  ; Outputs:
  7544                                  ;	IF DX != -1 on input (get country)
  7545                                  ;	  AL = 0 means return current country table.
  7546                                  ;	  0<AL<0FFH means return country table for country AL
  7547                                  ;	  AL = 0FF means return country table for country BX
  7548                                  ;	  No Carry:
  7549                                  ;	     Register BX will contain the 16-bit country code.
  7550                                  ;	     Register AL will contain the low 8 bits of the country code.
  7551                                  ;	     The block pointed to by DS:DX is filled in with the information
  7552                                  ;	     for the particular country.
  7553                                  ;		BYTE  Size of this table excluding this byte and the next
  7554                                  ;		BYTE  Country code represented by this table
  7555                                  ;			A sequence of n bytes, where n is the number specified
  7556                                  ;			by the first byte above and is not > internat_block_max,
  7557                                  ;			in the correct order for being returned by the
  7558                                  ;			INTERNATIONAL call as follows:
  7559                                  ;		WORD	Date format 0=mdy, 1=dmy, 2=ymd
  7560                                  ;		5 BYTE	Currency symbol null terminated
  7561                                  ;		2 BYTE	thousands separator null terminated
  7562                                  ;		2 BYTE	Decimal point null terminated
  7563                                  ;		2 BYTE	Date separator null terminated
  7564                                  ;		2 BYTE	Time separator null terminated
  7565                                  ;		1 BYTE	Bit field.  Currency format.
  7566                                  ;			Bit 0.	=0 $ before #  =1 $ after #
  7567                                  ;			Bit 1.	no. of spaces between # and $ (0 or 1)
  7568                                  ;		1 BYTE	No. of significant decimal digits in currency
  7569                                  ;		1 BYTE	Bit field.  Time format.
  7570                                  ;			Bit 0.	=0 12 hour clock  =1 24 hour
  7571                                  ;		DWORD	Call address of case conversion routine
  7572                                  ;		2 BYTE	Data list separator null terminated.
  7573                                  ;	  Carry:
  7574                                  ;	     Register AX has the error code.
  7575                                  ;	IF DX = -1 on input (set current country)
  7576                                  ;	  AL = 0 is an error
  7577                                  ;	  0<AL<0FFH means set current country to country AL
  7578                                  ;	  AL = 0FF means set current country to country BX
  7579                                  ;	  No Carry:
  7580                                  ;	    Current country SET
  7581                                  ;	    Register AL will contain the low 8 bits of the country code.
  7582                                  ;	  Carry:
  7583                                  ;	     Register AX has the error code.
  7584                                  ;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  7858                                  ;
  7859                                  ; Procedure Name : $GetExtCntry
  7860                                  ;

  7865                                  ;	      22H    capitalize ASCIIZ string

  7868                                  ;		      1 = use file upper case table

  9262                                  
  9263                                  ;BREAK <$Parse_File_Descriptor -- Parse an arbitrary string into an FCB>
  9264                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9265                                  ; Inputs:
  9266                                  ;       DS:SI Points to a command line
  9267                                  ;       ES:DI Points to an empty FCB
  9268                                  ;       Bit 0 of AL = 1 At most one leading separator scanned off
  9269                                  ;                   = 0 Parse stops if separator encountered
  9270                                  ;       Bit 1 of AL = 1 If drive field blank in command line - leave FCB
  9271                                  ;                   = 0  "    "    "     "         "      "  - put 0 in FCB
  9272                                  ;       Bit 2 of AL = 1 If filename field blank - leave FCB
  9273                                  ;                   = 0  "       "      "       - put blanks in FCB
  9274                                  ;       Bit 3 of AL = 1 If extension field blank - leave FCB
  9275                                  ;                   = 0  "       "      "        - put blanks in FCB
  9276                                  ; Function:
  9277                                  ;       Parse command line into FCB
  9278                                  ; Returns:
  9279                                  ;       AL = 1 if '*' or '?' in filename or extension, 0 otherwise
  9280                                  ;       DS:SI points to first character after filename
  9281                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9282                                  
  9283                                  	; 13/01/2024
  9284                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:51BFh
  9285                                  	; MSDOS 6.22 MSDOS.SYS - DOSCODE:4D22h
  9286                                  
  9287                                  _$PARSE_FILE_DESCRIPTOR:
  9288 000012A5 E8EE45                  	call	MAKEFCB
  9289 000012A8 56                      	PUSH    SI
  9290 000012A9 E8DFF1                  	call	Get_User_Stack
  9291                                  	;pop	word [si+8]
  9292 000012AC 8F4408                  	POP     word [SI+user_env.user_SI]
  9293 000012AF C3                      	retn
  9294

  9296                                  ; 13/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0 (PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:51CAh)

 10057                                  	inc	bx
 10058                                  	;INC	AX			; +2 (reserved), -1 (count -> max)
 10059                                  ;
 10060                                  ;	There has been a bug in our fatsize calculation for so long
 10061                                  ;	  that we can't correct it now without causing some user to
 10062                                  ;	  experience data loss. There are even cases where allowing
 10063                                  ;	  the number of clusters to exceed the fats is the optimal
 10064                                  ;	  case -- where adding 2 more fat sectors would make the
 10065                                  ;	  data field smaller so that there's nothing to use the extra
 10066                                  ;	  fat sectors for.
 10067                                  ;
 10068                                  ;	Note that this bug had very minor known symptoms. CHKDSK would
 10069                                  ;	  still report that there was a cluster left when the disk was
 10070                                  ;	  actually full. Very graceful failure for a corrupt system
 10071                                  ;	  configuration. There may be worse cases that were never
 10072                                  ;	  properly traced back to this bug. The problem cases only
 10073                                  ;	  occurred when partition sizes were very near FAT sector
 10074                                  ;	  rounding boundaries, which were rare cases.
 10075                                  ;
 10076                                  ;	Also, it's possible that some third-party partition program might
 10077                                  ;	  create a partition that had a less-than-perfect FAT calculation
 10078                                  ;	  scheme. In this hypothetical case, the number of allocation
 10079                                  ;	  clusters which don't actually have FAT entries to represent
 10080                                  ;	  them might be larger and might create a more catastrophic
 10081                                  ;	  failure. So we'll provide the safeguard of limiting the
 10082                                  ;	  max_cluster to the amount that will fit in the FATs.
 10083                                  ;
 10084                                  ;	ax = maximum legal cluster, ES:BP -> dpb
 10085                                  
 10086                                  ;	make sure the number of fat sectors is actually enough to
 10087                                  ;	  hold that many clusters. otherwise, back the number of
 10088                                  ;	  clusters down
 10089                                  
 10090                                  	; 15/12/2022
 10091                                  	; bx = number of clusters
 10092                                  
 10093                                  	; 19/07/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0

 10095                                  	; 15/12/2022

 10697                                  	; (MSDOS 6.0 note)
 10698                                  	;
 10699                                  	; The address in BX:AX will be F01D:FEF0 if there is 64K or more 
 10700                                  	; memory in the system. This is equivalent to 0:c0 if A20 is OFF.
 10701                                  	; If DOS is in HMA this equivalence is no longer valid as A20 is ON.
 10702                                  	; But the BIOS which now resides in FFFF:30 has 5 bytes in FFFF:D0
 10703                                  	; (F01D:FEF0) which is the same as the ones in 0:C0, thereby 
 10704                                  	; making this equvalence valid for this particular case. If however
 10705                                  	; there is less than 64K remaining the address in BX:AX will not 
 10706                                  	; be the same as above. We will then stuff 0:c0, the call 5 address
 10707                                  	; into the PSP.
 10708                                  	;
 10709                                  	; Therefore for the case where there is less than 64K remaining in 
 10710                                  	; the system old CPM Apps that look at PSP:6 to determine memory
 10711                                  	; requirements will not work. Call 5, however will continue to work
 10712                                  	; for all cases.
 10713                                  	;
 10714                                  
 10715                                  	;mov	[6],ax
 10716                                  	;mov	[8],bx

 10725                                  					;    OK
 10726                                  					; N:

 10892                                  ;
 10893                                  ;   Strcmp - compare ASCIZ DS:SI to ES:DI. Case INSENSITIVE. '/' = '\'
 10894                                  ;	     Strings of different lengths don't match.
 10895                                  ;   Inputs:  DS:SI - pointer to source string  ES:DI - pointer to dest string

 11447                                  ; Sleaze for time savings: first instruction is a return. This is patched
 11448                                  ; by the sharer to be a PUSH AX to complete the correct routines.
 11449                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

 11451                                  ; (DOSMAC.INC, MSDOS 6.0, 1991)
 11452                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 11453                                  ; Some old versions of the 80286 have a bug in the chip. The popf instruction
 11454                                  ; will enable interrupts. Therefore in a section of code with interrupts
 11455                                  ; disabled and you need a popf instruction use the 'popff' macro instead.
 11456                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 11457                                  
 11458                                  ;%macro POPFF 0
 11459                                  ;	jmp	$+3
 11460                                  ;	iret
 11461                                  ;	push	cs
 11462                                  ;	call	$-2
 11463                                  ;%endmacro

 11926                                  ;**	Standard device IO for MSDOS (first 12 function calls)
 11927                                  ;
 11928                                  ;	TITLE	IBMCPMIO - device IO for MSDOS
 11929                                  ;	NAME	IBMCPMIO
 11930                                  
 11931                                  ;	Old style CP/M 1-12 system calls to talk to reserved devices
 11932                                  ;
 11933                                  ;	$Std_Con_Input_No_Echo
 11934                                  ;	$Std_Con_String_Output
 11935                                  ;	$Std_Con_String_Input
 11936                                  ;	$RawConIO
 11937                                  ;	$RawConInput
 11938                                  ;	RAWOUT
 11939                                  ;	RAWOUT2
 11940                                  ;
 11941                                  
 11942                                  ; The following routines form the console I/O group (funcs 1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11).
 11943                                  ; They assume ES and DS NOTHING, while not strictly correct, this forces data
 11944                                  ; references to be SS or CS relative which is desired.

 11975                                  ; They assume ES and DS NOTHING, while not strictly correct, this forces data

 12001                                  ;	None
 12002                                  ; Function:

 12004                                  ; Returns:

 12011 000018DF 753A                    	jnz	short GET ; 08/09/2018

 12013                                  ;hkn; SS override
 12014 000018E1 36803E[A00A]00          	cmp	byte [SS:PRINTER_FLAG],0  ; is printer idle?

 12020 000018EE B484                    	MOV	AH,84h		; (Microsoft Networks - KEYBOARD BUSY LOOP)

 12055                                  ;	push	bx

 12119                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12120                                  ;
 12121                                  ;**	$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT - Input Line from Console
 12122                                  ;
 12123                                  ;	$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT Fills a buffer from console input until CR
 12124                                  ;
 12125                                  ;	ENTRY	(ds:dx) = input buffer
 12126                                  ;	EXIT	none
 12127                                  ;	USES	ALL
 12128                                  ;
 12129                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12130                                  
 12131                                  	; 15/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
 12132                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:58D4h
 12133                                  
 12134                                  _$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT:		;System call 10
 12135                                  
 12136                                  	; 15/01/2024
 12137                                  	;mov	ax,ss
 12138                                  	;mov	es,ax
 12139 0000193E 16                      	push	ss
 12140 0000193F 07                      	pop	es
 12141                                  
 12142 00001940 89D6                    	mov	si,dx
 12143 00001942 30ED                    	xor	ch,ch
 12144 00001944 AD                      	lodsw
 12145                                  
 12146                                  ;	(AL) = the buffer length
 12147                                  ;	(AH) = the template length
 12148                                  
 12149 00001945 08C0                            or	al,al
 12150 00001947 74E8                            jz	short noscan	;Buffer is 0 length!!?
 12151 00001949 88E3                    	mov	bl,ah		;Init template counter
 12152 0000194B 88EF                            mov	bh,ch		;Init template counter
 12153                                  
 12154                                  ;	(BL) = the number of bytes in the template
 12155                                  
 12156 0000194D 38D8                            cmp	al,bl
 12157 0000194F 7605                            jbe	short NOEDIT	;If length of buffer inconsistent with contents
 12158 00001951 80380D                          cmp	byte [bx+si],c_CR ; 0Dh
 12159 00001954 7402                            jz	short EDITON	;If CR correctly placed EDIT is OK
 12160                                  
 12161                                  ; The number of chars in the template is >= the number of chars in buffer or
 12162                                  ; there is no CR at the end of the template. This is an inconsistant state
 12163                                  ; of affairs. Pretend that the template was empty:
 12164                                  ;
 12165                                  
 12166                                  NOEDIT:	
 12167 00001956 88EB                    	mov	bl,ch		;Reset buffer
 12168                                  EDITON: 
 12169 00001958 88C2                    	mov	dl,al
 12170 0000195A 4A                      	dec	dx		;DL is # of bytes we can put in the buffer
 12171                                  
 12172                                  ;	Top level. We begin to read a line in.
 12173                                  
 12174                                  NEWLIN: 
 12175 0000195B 36A0[F901]              	mov	al,[SS:CARPOS]
 12176 0000195F 36A2[FA01]              	mov	[SS:STARTPOS],al ;Remember position in raw buffer
 12177                                  
 12178 00001963 56                      	push	si
 12179 00001964 BF[FB01]                	mov	di,INBUF ;Build the new line here
 12180 00001967 36882E[7905]            	mov	byte [SS:INSMODE],ch ;Insert mode off
 12181 0000196C 88EF                    	mov	bh,ch		;No chars from template yet
 12182 0000196E 88EE                    	mov	dh,ch		;No chars to new line yet
 12183 00001970 E867FF                  	call	_$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO ;Get first char
 12184 00001973 3C0A                    	cmp	al,c_LF		; 0Ah	;Linefeed 
 12185 00001975 7503                    	jnz	short GOTCH
 12186                                  
 12187                                  ;	This is the main loop of reading in a character and processing it.
 12188                                  ;
 12189                                  ;	(BH) = the index of the next byte in the template
 12190                                  ;	(BL) = the length of the template
 12191                                  ;	(DH) = the number of bytes in the buffer
 12192                                  ;	(DL) = the length of the buffer
 12193                                  
 12194                                  GETCH:
 12195 00001977 E860FF                  	call	_$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO
 12196                                  GOTCH:
 12197                                  ;
 12198                                  ; Brain-damaged Tim Patterson ignored ^F in case his BIOS did not flush the
 12199                                  ; input queue.
 12200                                  ;
 12201 0000197A 3C06                            cmp	al,"F"-"@"  ; CMP AL, 6  ; Ignore ^F
 12202 0000197C 74F9                    	jz	short GETCH
 12203                                  
 12204                                  ;	If the leading char is the function-key lead byte
 12205                                  
 12206                                  	;cmp	al,[SS:ESCCHAR]
 12207                                  
 12208                                  	; 04/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 12209                                  
 12210                                  ;hkn; 	ESCCHAR is in TABLE seg (DOSCODE)
 12211                                  
 12212 0000197E 2E3A06[670A]            	CMP	AL,[cs:ESCCHAR]
 12213 00001983 7439                            jz	short ESCAPE	;change reserved keyword DBM 5-7-87
 12214                                  
 12215                                  ;	Rubout and ^H are both destructive backspaces.
 12216                                  
 12217 00001985 3C7F                            cmp	al,c_DEL ; 7FH
 12218                                          ;jz	short BACKSPJ
 12219                                          ; 15/01/2024
 12220 00001987 7466                    	je	short BACKSP
 12221 00001989 3C08                    	cmp	al,c_BS  ; 8
 12222                                          ;jz	short BACKSPJ
 12223                                          ; 15/01/2024
 12224 0000198B 7462                    	je	short BACKSP
 12225                                  
 12226                                  	; 04/05/2019 -	MSDOS 6.0, also MSDOS 6.21 has bug (bullshit) here.
 12227                                  	;		Two NOPs -instead of a JMP short, as two bytes-
 12228                                  	;	   	after CMP and a CMP again!
 12229                                  	;		
 12230                                  	;		-It would be better if they use a 'JMP short' to 
 12231                                  	;	      	DOSCODE:5279h from DOSCODE:5271h and leave NOPs
 12232                                  	;		between them. Then, they would be able use a patch
 12233                                  	;		between 5271h and 5279h when if it will be required.
 12234                                  	;		I think Tim Patterson would not do this CMP mistake!-
 12235                                  	;	
 12236                                  	; (MSDOS.SYS, from DOSCODE:5271h to DOSCODE:5279h)
 12237                                  
 12238                                  	; 08/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 12239                                  	;

 12241                                  
 12242                                  ;DOSCODE:526D	cmp     al, 8

 12254                                  	
 12255                                  	; 08/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 12256                                  	; DOSCODE:525Dh
 12257                                  
 12258                                  ; 16/12/2022
 12259                                  %if 0
 12260                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 12261                                  ;	^W deletes backward once and then backs up until a letter is before the
 12262                                  ;	cursor
 12263                                  
 12264                                  	CMP     AL,"W"-"@" ; 17h
 12265

 12267                                  ;	cause ^W to backup a word.

 12271                                  	NOP

 12285

 12287 0000198F 7430                            jz	short ENDLIN

 12292 00001993 7442                    	jz	short PHYCRLF

 12311                                  
 12312                                  SAVCH:	
 12313 0000199C 38D6                    	cmp	dh,dl
 12314 0000199E 7317                    	jnb	short BUFFUL		; buffer is full.
 12315 000019A0 AA                              stosb
 12316 000019A1 FEC6                    	inc	dh                      ; increment count in buffer.
 12317 000019A3 E8B702                  	call	BUFOUT			; Print control chars nicely
 12318                                  
 12319 000019A6 36803E[7905]00                  cmp	byte [SS:INSMODE], 0
 12320 000019AC 75C9                    	jnz	short GETCH		; insertmode => don't advance template
 12321 000019AE 38DF                            cmp	bh,bl

 12323 000019B2 46                              inc	si                      ; Skip to next char in template
 12324 000019B3 FEC7                            inc	bh                      ; remember position in template
 12325 000019B5 EBC0                            jmp	short GETCH

 12453                                  ; DOSCODE:52F3h (MSDOS 621, MSDOS.SYS)
 12454                                  
 12455                                  ; The user wants to throw away what he's typed in and wants to start over.
 12456                                  ; We print the backslash and then go to the next line and tab to the correct
 12457                                  ; spot to begin the buffered input.
 12458                                  
 12459                                  KILNEW:
 12460 000019DC B05C                            mov	al,'\'
 12461 000019DE E8E801                          call	OUTT            ;Print the CANCEL indicator

 12463                                  PUTNEW:

 12482                                  BackSpace:

 12484 000019FC 7419                    	jz	short OLDBAK	;No chars in line, do nothing to line
 12485 000019FE E85800                  	call	BACKUP          ;Do the backup
 12486 00001A01 268A05                  	mov	al,[es:di]	;Get the deleted char
 12487 00001A04 3C20                            cmp	al,20h	; ' '
 12488 00001A06 730F                    	jnb	short OLDBAK	;Was a normal char

 13471                                  ;Break <$Get_FCB_Position - set random record fields to current pos>
 13472                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13473                                  ;
 13474                                  ;   $Get_FCB_Position - look at an FCB, retrieve the current position from the
 13475                                  ;	extent and next record field and set the random record field to point
 13476                                  ;	to that record
 13477                                  ;
 13478                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:DX point to a possible extended FCB
 13479                                  ;   Outputs:	The random record field of the FCB is set to the current record
 13480                                  ;   Registers modified: all
 13481                                  ;
 13482                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13483                                  ;
 13484                                  
 13485                                  _$GET_FCB_POSITION:
 13486 00001CE4 E8FB04                  	call	GetExtended		; point to FCB
 13487 00001CE7 E8CC04                  	call	GetExtent		; DX:AX is current record
 13488                                  	;mov	[si+21h],ax
 13489 00001CEA 894421                  	MOV	[SI+SYS_FCB.RR],AX 	; drop in low order piece
 13490                                  	;mov	[si+23h],dl
 13491 00001CED 885423                  	MOV	[SI+SYS_FCB.RR+2],DL	; drop in high order piece
 13492                                  	;cmp	word [si+0Eh],64
 13493 00001CF0 837C0E40                	CMP	word [SI+SYS_FCB.RECSIZ],64
 13494 00001CF4 7303                    	JAE	short GetFCBBye
 13495                                  	;mov	[si+24h],dh
 13496 00001CF6 887424                  	MOV	[SI+SYS_FCB.RR+2+1],DH	; Set 4th byte only if record size < 64
 13497                                  GoodPath:	; 16/12/2022

 13812                                  ;

 13816                                  ;fren90:	
 13817                                  ;	;jmp	FCB_RET_ERR
 13818                                  ;	; 08/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 13819                                  ;	jmp	short fcb_close_err
 13820                                  
 13821                                  ;Break <Misbehavior fixers>
 13822                                  ;
 13823                                  ;   FCBs suffer from several problems. First, they are maintained in the
 13824                                  ;   user's space so he may move them at will. Second, they have a small
 13825                                  ;   reserved area that may be used for system information. Third, there was
 13826                                  ;   never any "rules for behavior" for FCBs; there was no protocol for their
 13827                                  ;   usage.
 13828                                  ;
 13829                                  ;   This results in the following misbehavior:
 13830                                  ;
 13831                                  ;	infinite opens of the same file:
 13832                                  ;
 13833                                  ;	While (TRUE) {			While (TRUE) {
 13834                                  ;	    FCBOpen (FCB);		    FCBOpen (FCB);
 13835                                  ;	    Read (FCB); 		    Write (FCB);
 13836                                  ;	    }				    }
 13837                                  ;
 13838                                  ;	infinite opens of different files:
 13839                                  ;
 13840                                  ;	While (TRUE) {			While (TRUE) {
 13841                                  ;	    FCBOpen (FCB[i++]); 	    FCBOpen (FCB[i++]);
 13842                                  ;	    Read (FCB); 		    Write (FCB);
 13843                                  ;	    }				    }
 13844                                  ;
 13845                                  ;	multiple closes of the same file:
 13846                                  ;
 13847                                  ;	FCBOpen (FCB);
 13848                                  ;	while (TRUE)
 13849                                  ;	    FCBClose (FCB);
 13850                                  ;
 13851                                  ;	I/O after closing file:
 13852                                  ;
 13853                                  ;	FCBOpen (FCB);
 13854                                  ;	while (TRUE) {
 13855                                  ;	    FCBWrite (FCB);
 13856                                  ;	    FCBClose (FCB);
 13857                                  ;	    }
 13858                                  ;
 13859                                  ;   The following is am implementation of a methodology for emulating the
 13860                                  ;   above with the exception of I/O after close. We are NOT attempting to
 13861                                  ;   resolve that particular misbehavior. We will enforce correct behaviour in
 13862                                  ;   FCBs when they refer to a network file or when there is file sharing on
 13863                                  ;   the local machine.
 13864                                  ;
 13865                                  ;   The reserved fields of the FCB (10 bytes worth) is divided up into various
 13866                                  ;   structures depending on the file itself and the state of operations of the
 13867                                  ;   OS. The information contained in this reserved field is enough to
 13868                                  ;   regenerate the SFT for the local non-shared file. It is assumed that this
 13869                                  ;   regeneration procedure may be expensive. The SFT for the FCB is
 13870                                  ;   maintained in a LRU cache as the ONLY performance inprovement.
 13871                                  ;
 13872                                  ;   No regeneration of SFTs is attempted for network FCBs.
 13873                                  ;
 13874                                  ;   To regenerate the SFT for a local FCB, it is necessary to determine if the
 13875                                  ;   file sharer is working. If the file sharer is present then the SFT is not
 13876                                  ;   regenerated.
 13877                                  ;
 13878                                  ;   Finally, if there is no local sharing, the full name of the file is no
 13879                                  ;   longer available. We can make up for this by using the following
 13880                                  ;   information:
 13881                                  ;
 13882                                  ;	The Drive number (from the DPB).
 13883                                  ;	The physical sector of the directory that contains the entry.
 13884                                  ;	The relative position of the entry in the sector.
 13885                                  ;	The first cluster field.
 13886                                  ;	The last used SFT.
 13887                                  ;      OR In the case of a device FCB
 13888                                  ;	The low 6 bits of sf_flags (indicating device type)
 13889                                  ;	The pointer to the device header
 13890                                  ;
 13891                                  ;   We read in the particular directory sector and examine the indicated
 13892                                  ;   directory entry. If it matches, then we are kosher; otherwise, we fail.
 13893                                  ;
 13894                                  ;   Some key items need to be remembered:
 13895                                  ;
 13896                                  ;	Even though we are caching SFTs, they may contain useful sharing
 13897                                  ;	information. We enforce good behavior on the FCBs.
 13898                                  ;
 13899                                  ;	Network support must not treat FCBs as impacting the ref counts on
 13900                                  ;	open VCs. The VCs may be closed only at process termination.
 13901                                  ;
 13902                                  ;	If this is not an installed version of the DOS, file sharing will
 13903                                  ;	always be present.
 13904                                  ;
 13905                                  ;	We MUST always initialize lstclus to = firclus when regenerating a
 13906                                  ;	file. Otherwise we start allocating clusters up the wazoo.
 13907                                  ;
 13908                                  ;	Always initialize, during regeneration, the mode field to both isFCB
 13909                                  ;	and open_for_both. This is so the FCB code in the sharer can find the
 13910                                  ;	proper OI record.
 13911                                  ;
 13912                                  ;   The test bits are:
 13913                                  ;
 13914                                  ;	00 -> local file
 13915                                  ;	40 -> sharing local
 13916                                  ;	80 -> network
 13917                                  ;	C0 -> local device
 13918                                  
 13919                                  ;Break	<SaveFCBInfo - store pertinent information from an SFT into the FCB>
 13920                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13921                                  ;
 13922                                  ;   SaveFCBInfo - given an FCB and its associated SFT, copy the relevant
 13923                                  ;	pieces of information into the FCB to allow for subsequent
 13924                                  ;	regeneration. Poke LRU also.
 13925                                  ;
 13926                                  ;   Inputs:	ThisSFT points to a complete SFT.
 13927                                  ;		DS:SI point to the FCB (not an extended one)
 13928                                  ;   Outputs:	The relevant reserved fields in the FCB are filled in.
 13929                                  ;		DS:SI preserved
 13930                                  ;		ES:DI point to sft
 13931                                  ;   Registers modified: All
 13932                                  ;
 13933                                  ;
 13934                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13935                                  ;
 13936                                  
 13937                                  	; 08/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 13938                                  	; 20/01/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0 (Modified PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)
 13939                                  	
 13940                                  SaveFCBInfo:
 13941                                  
 13942 00001E00 36C43E[9E05]            	LES	DI,[SS:THISSFT]		; SS override
 13943 00001E05 E80DFA                  	call	IsSFTNet
 13944 00001E08 740B                    	JZ	short SaveLocal		; if not network then save local info
 13945                                  ;
 13946                                  ;----- In net support -----
 13947                                  ;
 13948                                  	; 17/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 13949                                  
 13950                                  	; MSDOS 3.3
 13951                                  	;;mov	ax,[es:di+1Dh]
 13952                                  	;mov	ax,[es:di+SF_ENTRY.sf_dirsec]
 13953                                  	;;mov	[si+1Ah],ax
 13954                                  	;mov	[si+fcb_net_handle],ax
 13955                                  	;push	es
 13956                                  	;push	di
 13957                                  	;;les	di,[es:di+19h]
 13958                                  	;LES	DI,[ES:DI+sf_netid]
 13959                                  	;;mov	[si+1Ch],di
 13960                                  	;MOV	[SI+fcb_netID],DI	; save net ID
 13961                                  	;;mov 	[si+1Eh],es
 13962                                  	;MOV	[SI+fcb_netID+2],ES
 13963                                  	;pop	di
 13964                                  	;pop	es
 13965

 14461                                  ; 17/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 14462                                  ; LRUFCB for MSDOS 6.0 !
 14463                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 14464                                  ;
 14465                                  ; LruFCB -- allocate the LRU SFT from the SFT Table. The LRU scheme
 14466                                  ; maintains separate counts for net/Share and local SFTs. We allocate a 
 14467                                  ; net/Share SFT only if we do not find a local SFT. This helps keep
 14468                                  ; net/Share SFTs which cannot be regenerated for as long as possible. We
 14469                                  ; optimize regeneration operations by keeping track of the current local
 14470                                  ; SFT. This avoids scanning of the SFTs as long as we have at least one 
 14471                                  ; local SFT in the SFT Block.
 14472                                  ;
 14473                                  ; Inputs: al = 0 => Regenerate SFT operation
 14474                                  ;	    = 1 => Allocate new SFT for Open/Create
 14475                                  ;
 14476                                  ; Outputs: Carry clear
 14477                                  ;	 	es:di = Address of allocated SFT
 14478                                  ;	  	ThisSFT = Address of allocated SFT
 14479                                  ;
 14480                                  ;	  carry set if closes of net/Share files failed 
 14481                                  ;		al = error_FCB_unavailable
 14482                                  ;
 14483                                  ; Registers affected: None
 14484                                  ;
 14485                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 14486                                  
 14487                                  ;LruFCB	PROC	NEAR
 14488                                  LRUFCB:
 14489                                  	; 17/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 14490                                  	; DOSCODE:5805h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 14491

 14494

 14538                                  	; We scan through all the SFTs scanning for a free one. It also

 14803                                  	; called from SFTFromFCB. SS already DOSDATA
 14804

 14817                                  
 14818                                  	; The FCB is for a network or a sharing based system. At this point 
 14819                                  	; we have already closed the SFT for this guy and reconnection is 
 14820                                  	; impossible.
 14821                                  	;

 14823                                  	; it. Check to see if sharing is present or if the redir is present.

 14825                                  	; give the hard error. Otherwise, just return with carry set.

 14833                                  			; Return: AL = 00h  not installed, OK to install
 14834                                  			; 01h  not installed, not OK to install
 14835                                  			; FFh  installed
 14836 00001FC3 08C0                    	OR	AL,AL			; is it there?

 15368                                  ;Break	<SFTFromFCB - take a FCB and obtain a SFT from it>
 15369                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15370                                  ;
 15371                                  ;   SFTFromFCB - the workhorse of this compatability crap. Check to see if
 15372                                  ;	the SFT for the FCB is Good. If so, make ThisSFT point to it. If not
 15373                                  ;	good, get one from the cache and regenerate it. Overlay the LRU field
 15374                                  ;	with PID
 15375                                  ;
 15376                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:SI point to FCB
 15377                                  ;   Outputs:	ThisSFT point to appropriate SFT

 15519                                  ;Break <GetRR - return the random record field in DX:AX>
 15520                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15521                                  ;
 15522                                  ;   GetRR - correctly load DX:AX with the random record field (3 or 4 bytes)
 15523                                  ;	from the FCB pointed to by DS:SI
 15524                                  ;
 15525                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:SI point to an FCB
 15526                                  ;		BX has record size
 15527                                  ;   Outputs:	DX:AX contain the contents of the random record field
 15528                                  ;   Registers modified: none
 15529                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15530                                  
 15531                                  GetRR:
 15532                                  	;mov	ax,[si+21h]
 15533 000021A8 8B4421                  	MOV	AX,[SI+SYS_FCB.RR]	; get low order part
 15534                                  	;mov	dx,[si+23h]
 15535 000021AB 8B5423                  	MOV	DX,[SI+SYS_FCB.RR+2]	; get high order part
 15536 000021AE 83FB40                  	CMP	BX,64			; ignore MSB of RR if recsiz > 64
 15537 000021B1 7202                    	JB	short GetRRBye
 15538                                  GetExtent_bye:	; 21/01/2024
 15539 000021B3 30F6                    	XOR	DH,DH
 15540                                  GetRRBye:
 15541 000021B5 C3                      	retn

 15543                                  ;Break <GetExtent - retrieve next location for sequential IO>
 15544                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15545                                  ;
 15546                                  ;   GetExtent - Construct the next record to perform I/O from the EXTENT and
 15547                                  ;	NR fields in the FCB.
 15548                                  ;
 15549                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:SI - point to FCB
 15550                                  ;   Outputs:	DX:AX contain the contents of the random record field
 15551                                  ;   Registers modified: none
 15552                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15553                                  
 15554                                  GetExtent:
 15555                                  	;mov	al,[si+20h]
 15556 000021B6 8A4420                  	MOV	AL,[SI+SYS_FCB.NR]	; get low order piece
 15557                                  	;mov	dx,[si+0Ch]
 15558 000021B9 8B540C                  	MOV	DX,[SI+SYS_FCB.EXTENT]	; get high order piece
 15559 000021BC D0E0                    	SHL	AL,1
 15560 000021BE D1EA                    	SHR	DX,1
 15561 000021C0 D0D8                    	RCR	AL,1	; move low order bit of DL to high order of AH
 15562 000021C2 88D4                    	MOV	AH,DL
