 43035                                  ;	BREAK <JFNFree - return a jfn pointer if one is free>
 43036                                  
 43037                                  ;**	JFNFree - Find a Free JFN Slot
 43038                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 43039                                  ;	JFNFree scansthrough the JFN table and returnsa pointer to a free slot
 43040                                  ;
 43041                                  ;	ENTRY	(ss) = DOSDATA
 43042                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if OK
 43043                                  ;		  (bx) = new handle
 43044                                  ;		  (es:di) = pointer to JFN slot
 43045                                  ;		'C' set if error
 43046                                  ;		  (al) = error code
 43047                                  ;	USES	bx, di, es, flags
 43048                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 43049                                  
 43050                                  JFNFree:
 43051 00007323 31DB                    	XOR	BX,BX			; (bx) = initial JFN to try
 43052                                  jfnf1:	
 43053 00007325 E89EFF                  	CALL	pJFNFromHandle		; get the appropriate handle
 43054 00007328 7209                    	JC	short jfnf5		; no more handles
 43055 0000732A 26803DFF                	CMP     BYTE [ES:DI],-1		; free?
 43056 0000732E 7405                    	je	short jfnfx		; yes, carry is clear
 43057 00007330 43                      	INC     BX                      ; no, next handle
 43058 00007331 EBF2                    	JMP	short jfnf1		; and try again
 43059                                  
 43060                                  	; Error. 'C' set
 43061                                  jfnf5:	
 43062                                  	;mov	al,4
 43063 00007333 B004                    	MOV	AL,error_too_many_open_files
 43064                                  jfnfx:	
 43065 00007335 C3                      	retn				; bye
 43066                                  
 43067                                  ;	BREAK <SFNFree - Allocate a free SFN>
 43068                                  
 43069                                  ;**	SFNFree - Allocate a Free SFN/SFT
 43070                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 43071                                  ;	SFNFree scans through the sf table looking for a free entry
 43072                                  ;	If it finds one it partially allocates it by setting SFT_REF_COUNT = -1
 43073                                  ;
 43074                                  ;	The problem is that we want to mark the SFT busy so that other threads
 43075                                  ;	can't allocate the SFT before we're finished marking it up.  However,
 43076                                  ;	we can't just mark it busy because we may get blown out of our open
 43077                                  ;	by INT24 and leave the thing orphaned.	To solve this we mark it
 43078                                  ;	"allocation in progress" by setting SFT_REF_COUNT = -1.  If we see
 43079                                  ;	an SFT with this value we look to see if it belongs to this user
 43080                                  ;	and process.  If it does belong to us then it must be an orphan
 43081                                  ;	and we reclaim it.
 43082                                  ;
 43083                                  ;	BUGBUG - improve the performance. I guess it's smaller to call SFFromSFN
 43084                                  ;		over and over, but we could at least set a high water mark...
 43085                                  ;		cause an N^2 loop calling slow SFFromSFN is real slow, too slow
 43086                                  ;		even though this is not a frequently called routine - jgl
 43087                                  ;
 43088                                  ;	ENTRY	(ss) = DOSDATA
 43089                                  ;	EXIT	'C' clear if no error
 43090                                  ;		  (bx) = SFN
 43091                                  ;		  (es:di) = pointer to SFT
 43092                                  ;		  es:[di].SFT_REF_COUNT = -1
 43093                                  ;		'C' set if error
 43094                                  ;		  (al) = error code
 43095                                  ;	USES	bx, di, es, Flags
 43096                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 43097                                  
 43098                                  	; 02/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 43099                                  	; DOSCODE:A682h (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 43100                                  
 43101                                  	; 11/03/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0 (Modified PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)
 43102                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:0B8DEh
 43103                                  
 43104                                  SFNFree:
 43105                                  	; 12/08/2018
 43106                                  	; 05/08/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 43107                                  	;
 43108                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 43109 00007336 50                      	push	ax
 43110 00007337 31DB                    	xor	bx,bx			; (bx) = SFN to consider
 43111                                  sfnf5:	
 43112 00007339 53                      	push	bx
 43113 0000733A E8BCFF                  	call	SFFromSFN		; get the potential handle
 43114 0000733D 5B                      	pop	bx
 43115 0000733E 723A                    	jc	short sfnf95		; no more free SFNs
 43116 00007340 26833D00                	cmp	word [ES:DI],0
 43117                                  	;cmp	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_Ref_Count],0 ; free?
 43118 00007344 741D                    	je	short sfnf20			; yep, got one
 43119                                  	
 43120                                  	;cmp	word [es:di],0FFFFh ; -1
 43121 00007346 26833DFF                	cmp	word [ES:DI],sf_busy
 43122                                  	;cmp	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],sf_busy
 43123 0000734A 7403                    	je	short sfnf10		; special busy mark
 43124                                  sfnf7:	
 43125 0000734C 43                      	inc	bx			; try the next one
 43126 0000734D EBEA                    	jmp	short sfnf5
 43127                                  
 43128                                  ;	The SFT has the special "busy" mark; if it belongs to us then
 43129                                  ;	it was abandoned during a earlier call and we can use it.
 43130                                  ;
 43131                                  ;	(bx)	= SFN
 43132                                  ;	(es:di) = pointer to SFT
 43133                                  ;	(TOS)	= caller's (ax)
 43134                                  
 43135                                  sfnf10:	
 43136 0000734F 36A1[3E03]              	mov	ax,[SS:USER_ID]
 43137                                  	;cmp	[es:di+2Fh],ax
 43138 00007353 2639452F                	cmp	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_UID],ax
 43139 00007357 75F3                    	jnz	short sfnf7		; not ours
 43140 00007359 36A1[3C03]              	mov	ax,[SS:PROC_ID]
 43141                                  	;cmp	[es:di+31h],ax
 43142 0000735D 26394531                	cmp	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_PID],ax
 43143 00007361 75E9                    	jnz	short sfnf7		; can't use this one, try the next
 43144                                  
 43145                                  ;	We have an SFT to allocate
 43146                                  ;
 43147                                  ;	(bx)	= SFN
 43148                                  ;	(es:di) = pointer to SFT
 43149                                  ;	(TOS)	= caller's (ax)
 43150                                  
 43151                                  sfnf20:
 43152                                  	; cf = 0 ;; Retro DOS v3.0
 43153                                  
 43154                                  	;mov	word [es:di],0FFFFh
 43155 00007363 26C705FFFF              	mov	word [ES:DI],sf_busy
 43156                                  					; make sure that this is allocated
 43157                                  	;mov	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count],sf_busy
 43158                                  
 43159 00007368 36A1[3E03]              	mov	ax,[SS:USER_ID]
 43160                                  	;mov	[es:di+2Fh],ax
 43161 0000736C 2689452F                	mov	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_UID],ax
 43162 00007370 36A1[3C03]              	mov	ax,[SS:PROC_ID]
 43163                                  	;mov	[es:di+31h],ax
 43164 00007374 26894531                	mov	[ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_PID],ax
 43165                                  sfnf21: ;; Retro DOS v3.0
 43166                                  	; 02/12/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 43167                                  	;pop	ax
 43168                                  	;;clc
 43169                                  	;retn				; return with no error
 43170                                  	; 17/12/2022
 43171 00007378 58                      	pop	ax
 43172                                  	;clc
 43173 00007379 C3                      	retn
 43174                                  
 43175                                  ;**	Error - no more free SFNs
 43176                                  ;
 43177                                  ;	'C' set
 43178                                  ;	(TOS) = saved ax
 43179                                  
 43180                                  sfnf95: 
 43181 0000737A 58                      	pop	ax
 43182                                  
 43183                                  ; 11/03/2024
 43184                                  %if 0

 43188                                  %else

 43207                                  ;**	$Close - Close a file Handle

 43210                                  ;		path

 44335                                  ;Break	<CheckOwner - verify ownership of handles from server>
 44336                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 44337                                  ;   CheckOwner - Due to the ability of the server to close file handles for a
 44338                                  ;   process without the process knowing it (delete/rename of open files, for
 44339                                  ;   example), it is possible for the redirector to issue a call to a handle
 44340                                  ;   that it does not rightfully own. We check here to make sure that the
 44341                                  ;   issuing process is the owner of the SFT. At the same time, we do a
 44342                                  ;   SFFromHandle to really make sure that the SFT is good.
 44343                                  ;
 44344                                  ;	ENTRY	BX has the handle
 44345                                  ;		User_ID is the current user
 44346                                  ;	EXIT	Carry Clear => ES:DI points to SFT
 44347                                  ;		Carry Set => AX has error code
 44348                                  ;	USES	none
 44349                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 44400                                  ;	TITLE	MACRO - Pathname and macro related internal routines
 44401                                  ;	NAME	MACRO
 44402                                  
 44403                                  ;	Microsoft Confidential
 44404                                  ;	Copyright (C) Microsoft Corporation 1991
 44405                                  ;	All Rights Reserved.
 44406                                  
 44407                                  ;**	MACRO.ASM
 44408                                  ;
 44409                                  ;	$AssignOper
 44410                                  ;	FIND_DPB
 44411                                  ;	InitCDS
 44412                                  ;	$UserOper
 44413                                  ;	GetVisDrv
 44414                                  ;	GetThisDrv
 44415                                  ;	GetCDSFromDrv
 44416                                  ;
 44417                                  ;   Revision history:
 44418                                  ;
 44419                                  ;	Created: MZ 4 April 1983
 44420                                  ;		 MZ 18 April 1983   Make TransFCB handle extended FCBs
 44421                                  ;		 AR 2 June 1983     Define/Delete macro for NET redir.
 44422                                  ;		 MZ 3 Nov 83	    Fix InitCDS to reset length to 2
 44423                                  ;		 MZ 4 Nov 83	    Fix NetAssign to use STRLEN only
 44424                                  ;		 MZ 18 Nov 83	    Rewrite string processing for subtree
 44425                                  ;				    aliasing.
 44426                                  ;
 44427                                  ;   MSDOS performs several types of name translation. First, we maintain for
 44428                                  ;   each valid drive letter the text of the current directory on that drive.
 44429                                  ;   For invalid drive letters, there is no current directory so we pretend to
 44430                                  ;   be at the root. A current directory is either the raw local directory
 44431                                  ;   (consisting of drive:\path) or a local network directory (consisting of
 44432                                  ;   \\machine\path. There is a limit on the point to which a .. is allowed.
 44433                                  ;
 44434                                  ;   Given a path, MSDOS will transform this into a real from-the-root path
 44435                                  ;   without . or .. entries. Any component that is > 8.3 is truncated to
 44436                                  ;   this and all * are expanded into ?'s.
 44437                                  ;
 44438                                  ;   The second part of name translation involves subtree aliasing. A list of
 44439                                  ;   subtree pairs is maintained by the external utility SUBST. The results of
 44440                                  ;   the previous 'canonicalization' are then examined to see if any of the
 44441                                  ;   subtree pairs is a prefix of the user path. If so, then this prefix is
 44442                                  ;   replaced with the other subtree in the pair.
 44443                                  ;
 44444                                  ;   A third part involves mapping this "real" path into a "physical" path.  A
 44445                                  ;   list of drive/subtree pairs are maintained by the external utility JOIN.
 44446                                  ;   The output of the previous translation is examined to see if any of the
 44447                                  ;   subtrees in this list are a prefix of the string. If so, then the prefix
 44448                                  ;   is replaced by the appropriate drive letter. In this manner, we can
 44449                                  ;   'mount' one device under another.
 44450                                  ;
 44451                                  ;   The final form of name translation involves the mapping of a user's
 44452                                  ;   logical drive number into the internal physical drive. This is
 44453                                  ;   accomplished by converting the drive number into letter:CON, performing
 44454                                  ;   the above translation and then converting the character back into a drive
 44455                                  ;   number.
 44456                                  ;
 44457                                  ;   There are two main entry points: TransPath and TransFCB. TransPath will
 44458                                  ;   take a path and form the real text of the pathname with all . and ..
 44459                                  ;   removed. TransFCB will translate an FCB into a path and then invoke
 44460                                  ;   TransPath.
 44461                                  ;
 44462                                  ;	A000	version 4.00  Jan. 1988
 44463                                  
 44464                                  ;Installed = TRUE
 44465                                  
 44466                                  ;	I_need	ThisCDS,DWORD		; pointer to CDS used
 44467                                  ;	I_need	CDSAddr,DWORD		; pointer to CDS table
 44468                                  ;	I_need	CDSCount,BYTE		; number of CDS entries
 44469                                  ;	I_need	CurDrv,BYTE		; current macro assignment (old
 44470                                  ;					; current drive)
 44471                                  ;	I_need	NUMIO,BYTE		; Number of physical drives
 44472                                  ;	I_need	fSharing,BYTE		; TRUE => no redirection allowed
 44473                                  ;	I_need	DummyCDS,80h		; buffer for dummy cds
 44474                                  ;	I_need	DIFFNAM,BYTE		; flag for MyName being set
 44475                                  ;	I_need	MYNAME,16		; machine name
 44476                                  ;	I_need	MYNUM,WORD		; machine number
 44477                                  ;	I_need	DPBHEAD,DWORD		; beginning of DPB chain
 44478                                  ;	I_need	EXTERR_LOCUS,BYTE	; Extended Error Locus
 44479                                  ;	I_need	DrvErr,BYTE		; drive error

 45085                                  ; 12/07/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
 45086                                  
 45087                                  ;BREAK <TransPath - copy a path, do string sub and put in current dir>
 45088                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45089                                  ;
 45090                                  ;   TransPath - copy a path from DS:SI to ES:DI, performing component string
 45091                                  ;       substitution, insertion of current directory and fixing . and ..
 45092                                  ;       entries. Perform splicing. Allow input string to match splice
 45093                                  ;       exactly.
 45094                                  ;
 45095                                  ;   TransPathSet - Same as above except No splicing is performed if input path
 45096                                  ;       matches splice.
 45097                                  ;
 45098                                  ;   TransPathNoSet - No splicing/local using is performed at all.
 45099                                  ;
 45100                                  ;   The following anomalous behaviour is required:
 45101                                  ;
 45102                                  ;       Drive letters on devices are ignored. (set up DummyCDS)
 45103                                  ;       Paths on devices are ignored. (truncate to 0-length)
 45104                                  ;       Raw net I/O sets ThisCDS => NULL.
 45105                                  ;       fSharing => dummyCDS and no subst/splice. Only canonicalize.
 45106                                  ;
 45107                                  ;   Other behaviour:
 45108                                  ;
 45109                                  ;       ThisCDS set up.
 45110                                  ;       FatRead done on local CDS.
 45111                                  ;       ValidateCDS done on local CDS.
 45112                                  ;
 45113                                  ;   Brief flowchart:
 45114                                  ;
 45115                                  ;       if fSharing then
 45116                                  ;           set up DummyCDS (ThisCDS)
 45117                                  ;           canonicalize (sets cMeta)
 45118                                  ;           splice
 45119                                  ;           fatRead
 45120                                  ;           return
 45121                                  ;       if \\ or d:\\ lead then
 45122                                  ;           set up null CDS (ThisCDS)
 45123                                  ;           canonicalize (sets cMeta)
 45124                                  ;           return
 45125                                  ;       if device then
 45126                                  ;           set up dummyCDS (ThisCDS)
 45127                                  ;           canonicalize (sets cMeta)
 45128                                  ;           return
 45129                                  ;       if file then
 45130                                  ;           getCDS (sets (ThisCDS) from name)
 45131                                  ;           validateCDS (may reset current dir)
 45132                                  ;           Copy current dir
 45133                                  ;           canonicalize (set cMeta)
 45134                                  ;           splice
 45135                                  ;           generate correct CDS (ThisCDS)
 45136                                  ;           if local then
 45137                                  ;               fatread
 45138                                  ;           return
 45139                                  ;
 45140                                  ;   Inputs:     DS:SI - point to ASCIZ string path
 45141                                  ;               DI - point to buffer in DOSDATA
 45142                                  ;   Outputs:    Carry Set - invalid path specification: too many .., bad
 45143                                  ;                   syntax, etc. or user FAILed to I 24.
 45144                                  ;               WFP_Start - points to beginning of buffer
 45145                                  ;               Curr_Dir_End - points to end of current dir in path
 45146                                  ;               DS - DOSDATA
 45147                                  ;   Registers modified: most
 45148                                  ;
 45149                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45150                                  
 45151                                  ; 22/05/2019
 45152                                  ; 13/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 45153                                  ; DOSCODE:AB99h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 45154                                  
 45155                                  ; 04/12/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 45156                                  ; DOSCODE:AB39h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
 45157

 45915                                  ;Break <$NameTrans - partially process a name>
 45916                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45917                                  ;   $NameTrans - allow users to see what names get mapped to. This call
 45918                                  ;   performs only string substitution and canonicalization, not splicing.  Due
 45919                                  ;   to Transpath playing games with devices, we need to insure that the output
 45920                                  ;   has drive letter and : in it.
 45921                                  ;
 45922                                  ;   Inputs:     DS:SI - source string for translation
 45923                                  ;               ES:DI - pointer to buffer
 45924                                  ;   Outputs:
 45925                                  ;       Carry Clear
 45926                                  ;               Buffer at ES:DI is filled in with data
 45927                                  ;               ES:DI point byte after nul byte at end of dest string in buffer
 45928                                  ;       Carry Set
 45929                                  ;               AX = error_path_not_found
 45930                                  ;   Registers modified: all
 45931                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 45932                                  
 45933                                  _$NameTrans:
 45934 00007B74 1E                      	push	ds
 45935 00007B75 56                      	push	si
 45936 00007B76 06                      	push	es

 45938 00007B78 51                      	push	cx ; MSDOS 6.0
 45939                                  	
 45940                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 45941                                  ; M027 - Start
 45942                                  ;
 45943                                  ; Sattrib must be set up with default values here. Otherwise, the value from
 45944                                  ; a previous DOS call is used for attrib and DevName thinks it is not a 
 45945                                  ; device if the old call set the volume attribute bit. Note that devname in

 46749                                  ;**	BinToAscii - convert a number to a string.
 46750                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46751                                  ;	BinToAscii converts a 16 bit number into a 4 ascii characters.
 46752                                  ;	This routine is used to generate temp file names so we don't spend
 46753                                  ;	the time and code needed for a true hex number, we just use
 46754                                  ;	A thorugh O.
 46755                                  ;
 46756                                  ;	ENTRY	(ax) = value
 46757                                  ;		(es:di) = destination
 46758                                  ;	EXIT	(es:di) updated by 4
 46759                                  ;	USES	cx, di, flags
 46760                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46761                                  
 46762                                  ; MSDOS 3.3
 46763                                  ;BinToAscii:
 46764                                  ;	mov     cx,4
 46765                                  ;bta5:
 46766                                  ;	push    cx
 46767                                  ;	mov     cl,4
 46768                                  ;	rol     ax,cl
 46769                                  ;	push    ax
 46770                                  ;	and     al,0Fh
 46771                                  ;	add     al,'0'
 46772                                  ;	cmp     al,'9'
 46773                                  ;	jbe     short bta6
 46774                                  ;	add     al,7
 46775                                  ;bta6: 
 46776                                  ;	stosb
 46777                                  ;	pop     ax
 46778                                  ;	pop     cx
 46779                                  ;	loop    bta5
 46780                                  ;	retn
 46781                                  
 46782                                  ; 15/03/2024
 46783                                  ; MSDOS 5.0-6.22 & Windows ME
 46784                                  ; (MSDOS 6.22 MSDOS.SYS - DOSCODE:0B0D9h)
 46785                                  ; (Windows ME IO.SYS - BIOSCODE:0ABA4h)
 46786                                  %if 0
 46787                                  
 46788                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
 46789                                  BinToAscii:
 46790                                  	mov	cx,404h			; (ch) = digit counter, (cl) = shift cnt
 46791                                  bta5:	
 46792                                  	ROL	AX,CL			; move leftmost nibble into rightmost
 46793                                  	push	ax			; preserve remainder of digits
 46794                                  	AND	AL,0Fh			; grab low nibble
 46795                                  	ADD	AL,'A'			; turn into ascii
 46796                                  	STOSB				; drop in the character
 46797                                  	pop	ax			; (ax) = shifted number
 46798                                  	dec	ch
 46799                                  	jnz	short bta5		; process 4 digits
 46800                                  	retn
 46801                                  %else
 46802                                  ; 15/03/2024
 46803                                  ; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:0C385h
 46804                                  
 46805                                  BinToAscii:
 46806 00007DC4 50                      	push	ax		; convert a number to a string ; ax = value
 46807 00007DC5 86E0                    	xchg	ah,al
 46808                                  	;db	0D4h,10h
 46809 00007DC7 D410                    	aam	10h		; AH = AL / 16 and AL = remainder
 46810 00007DC9 054141                  	add	ax,4141h	; 'AA'
 46811 00007DCC AB                      	stosw
 46812 00007DCD 58                      	pop	ax

 46814 00007DCE D410                    	aam	10h

 46816 00007DD3 AB                      	stosw
 46817 00007DD4 C3                      	retn

 46853                                  ; vol_id and dir bits) because of the structure of the or $CreateNewFile loop

 47287                                  ;	    MOV     SI, LengthHigh

 47802                                  ;Break <ShareEnter - attempt to enter a node into the sharing set>
 47803                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47804                                  ;   ShareEnter - perform a retried entry of a nodde into the sharing set. If
 47805                                  ;   the max number of retries is exceeded, we notify the user via int 24.
 47806                                  ;
 47807                                  ;   Inputs:     ThisSFT points to the SFT
 47808                                  ;               WFP_Start points to the WFP
 47809                                  ;   Outputs:    Carry clear => successful entry
 47810                                  ;               Carry set => failed system call
 47811                                  ;   Registers modified: all
 47812                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47813                                  
 47814                                  ShareEnter:
 47815 00008099 51                      	push	cx
 47816                                  retry:
 47817 0000809A 8B0E[1A00]              	mov     cx,[RetryCount]
 47818                                  attempt:
 47819 0000809E C43E[9E05]              	les     di,[THISSFT]		; grab sft
 47820 000080A2 31C0                    	XOR     AX,AX
 47821                                   	;mov	[es:di+51],ax
 47822 000080A4 26894533                	MOV     [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_MFT],AX ; indicate free SFT
 47823 000080A8 51                      	push	cx
 47824 000080A9 E8ABFF                  	call    SHARE_CHECK             ; attempt to enter into the sharing set
 47825 000080AC 59                      	pop	cx
 47826 000080AD 730A                    	jnc	short done		; success, let the user see this
 47827 000080AF E80597                  	call	Idle                    ; wait a while
 47828 000080B2 E2EA                    	loop    attempt                 ; go back for another attempt
 47829 000080B4 E8A5FF                  	call    SHARE_VIOLATION         ; signal the problem to the user
 47830 000080B7 73E1                    	jnc	short retry		; user said to retry, go do it
 47831                                  done:
 47832 000080B9 59                      	pop	cx
 47833 000080BA C3                      	retn

 47842                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47843                                  ;	Contains the foll:
 47844                                  ;
 47845                                  ;		- code to find and overlay buggy unpack code

 47855                                  ;
 47856                                  ; M020 : Fix for rational bug - for details see routine header
 47857                                  ; M028 : 4b04 implementation
 47858                                  ; M030 : Fixing bug in EXEPACKPATCH (EXEC_CS is an un-relocated value)
 47859                                  ; M032 : set turnoff bit only if DOS in HMA.
 47860                                  ; M033 : if IP < 2 then not exepacked.
 47861                                  ; M046 : support for a 4th version of exepacked files.

 48064                                  ;
 48065                                  ; Procedure Name : WhatCPUType
 48066                                  ;
 48067                                  ; Inputs	 : none
 48068                                  ;
 48069                                  ; Outputs	 : AL = 0 if CPU <  286
 48070                                  ;		      = 1 if CPU == 286
 48071                                  ;		      = 2 if CPU >= 386
 48072                                  ;
 48073                                  ; Regs. Mod.	 : AX
 48074                                  ;
 48075                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 48076                                  
 48077                                  WhatCPUType:
 48078                                  	; 25/04/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 48079                                  	;get_cpu_type	; done with a MACRO which can't be generated > once
 48080                                  
 48081                                  	;CPUTYPE.INC (MSDOS 6.0, 1991)
 48082                                  
 48083                                  ; Note: this must be a macro, and not a subroutine in the BIOS since
 48084                                  ; 	it is called from both CODE and SYSINITSEG.
 48085                                  ;
 48086                                  ;------GET_CPU_TYPE-----------------------------------May, 88 by M.Williamson
 48087                                  ;  Returns: AX = 0 if 8086 or 8088
 48088                                  ;              = 1 if 80286
 48089                                  ;              = 2 if 80386
 48090                                  
 48091                                  	; 04/11/2022
 48092                                  	; MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS - DOSCODE:0BB03h
 48093                                  
 48094                                  	; 22/03/2024
 48095                                  	; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSCODE:0CCEDh
 48096                                  
 48097                                  Get_CPU_Type:	;macro
 48098 00008131 9C                      	pushf
 48099 00008132 53                      	push	bx			; preserve bx
 48100 00008133 31DB                    	xor	bx,bx			; init bx to zero
 48101                                  
 48102 00008135 31C0                    	xor	ax,ax			; 0000 into AX
 48103 00008137 50                      	push	ax			; put it on the stack...
 48104 00008138 9D                      	popf				; ...then shove it into the flags
 48105 00008139 9C                      	pushf				; get it back out of the flags...
 48106 0000813A 58                      	pop	ax			; ...and into ax
 48107 0000813B 2500F0                  	and	ax,0F000h		; mask off high four bits
 48108 0000813E 3D00F0                  	cmp	ax,0F000h		; was it all 1's?
 48109 00008141 740E                    	je	short cpu_8086		; aye; it's an 8086 or 8088
 48110                                  
 48111 00008143 B800F0                  	mov	ax,0F000h		; now try to set the high four bits..
 48112 00008146 50                      	push	ax
 48113 00008147 9D                      	popf
 48114 00008148 9C                      	pushf
 48115 00008149 58                      	pop	ax			; ...and see what happens
 48116 0000814A 2500F0                  	and	ax,0F000h		; any high bits set ?
 48117 0000814D 7401                    	jz	short cpu_286		; nay; it's an 80286
 48118                                  cpu_386:				; bx starts as zero
 48119 0000814F 43                      	inc	bx			; inc twice if 386
 48120                                  cpu_286:				; just inc once if 286
 48121 00008150 43                      	inc	bx
 48122                                  cpu_8086:				; don't inc at all if 086
 48123 00008151 89D8                    	mov	ax,bx			; put CPU type value in ax
 48124 00008153 5B                      	pop	bx			; restore original bx
 48125 00008154 9D                      	popf
 48126                                  	
 48127                                  	;endm
 48128                                  
 48129                                  	; 04/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
 48130 00008155 C3                      	retn	; 19/09/2023
 48131

 49134                                  ;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 49135                                  ;
 49136                                  ; Procedure Name : seg_reinit
 49137                                  ;
 49138                                  ; Inputs	 : ES has final dos code location
 49139                                  ;		   AX = 0 / 1
 49140                                  ;
 49141                                  ; Outputs	 : Patch in the sharer and other tables with seg in ES
 49142                                  ;		   if AX =0
 49143                                  ;		      if first entry
 49144                                  ;			 patch segment & offset of vectors with stub
 49145                                  ;			 and stub with segment in ES
 49146                                  ;		      else
 49147                                  ;			 patch stub with segment in ES
 49148                                  ;
 49149                                  ;		   else if AX = 1
 49150                                  ;			patch segment of vectors with segment in ES
 49151                                  ;
 49152                                  ; NOTE		 : This routine can be called at most twice!
 49153                                  ;
 49154                                  ; Regs Mod.	 : es, ax, di, cx, bx
 49155                                  ;-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 49156                                  
 49157 0000847E 00                      num_entry: db	0		; keeps track of the # of times this routine
 49158                                  				; has been called. (0 or 1)

 49904                                  ;;***************************************************************************
 49905                                  ;; INT 21,52 - Get Pointer to DOS "INVARS" (Undocumented)
 49906                                  ;;
 49907                                  ;;	AH = 52h
 49908                                  ;;
 49909                                  ;;	on return:
 49910                                  ;;	ES:BX = pointer to DOS "invars", a table of pointers used by DOS.
 49911                                  ;;		Known "invars" fields follow (varies with DOS version):
 49912                                  ;;
 49913                                  ;;	Offset Size		 Description
 49914                                  ;;
 49915                                  ;;	 -12   word   sharing retry count (DOS 3.1-3.3)
 49916                                  ;;	 -10   word   sharing retry delay  (DOS 3.1-3.3)
 49917                                  ;;	  -8   dword  pointer to current disk buffer (DOS 3.x)
 49918                                  ;;	  -4   word   pointer in DOS code segment of unread CON input;
 49919                                  ;;		      0 indicates no unread input (DOS 3.x)
 49920                                  ;;	  -2   word   segment of first Memory Control Block (MCB)
 49921                                  ;;	  00   dword  pointer to first DRIVE PARAMETER TABLE (A:) in chain
 49922                                  ;;	  04   dword  pointer to DOS System File Table (SFT)
 49923                                  ;;	  08   dword  pointer to $CLOCK device driver
 49924                                  ;;	  0C   dword  pointer to CON device driver
 49925                                  ;;	  10   byte   number of logical drives in system
 49926                                  ;;	  11   word   maximum bytes/block of any block device
 49927                                  ;;	  13   dword  pointer to DOS cache buffer header
 49928                                  ;;	  17 18bytes  NUL device header, first 4 bytes of device header
 49929                                  ;;		      point to the next device in device chain
 49930                                  ;;

 50144                                  
 50145                                  ;Break <Initialized data and data used at DOS initialization>
 50146                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 50147                                  
 50148                                  ; We need to identify the parts of the data area that are relevant to tasks
 50149                                  ; and those that are relevant to the system as a whole.  Under 3.0, the system
 50150                                  ; data will be gathered with the system code.  The process data under 2.x will
 50151                                  ; be available for swapping and under 3.0 it will be allocated per-process.
 50152                                  ;
 50153                                  ; The data that is system data will be identified by [SYSTEM] in the comments
 50154                                  ; describing that data item.
 50155                                  
 50156                                  ;DOSDATA SEGMENT WORD PUBLIC 'DATA'
 50157                                  
 50158                                  ;
 50159                                  ; Table of routines for assignable devices
 50160                                  ;
 50161                                  ; MSDOS allows assignment if the following standard devices:
 50162                                  ;   stdin  (usually CON input)
 50163                                  ;   stdout (usually CON output)
 50164                                  ;   auxin  (usually AUX input)
 50165                                  ;   auxout (usually AUX output)
 50166                                  ;   stdlpt (usually PRN output)
 50167                                  ;
 50168                                  ; SPECIAL NOTE:
 50169                                  ;   Status of a file is a strange idea. We choose to handle it in this manner:
 50170                                  ;   If we're not at end-of-file, then we always say that we have a character.
 50171                                  ;   Otherwise, we return ^Z as the character and set the ZERO flag. In this
 50172                                  ;   manner we can support program written under the old DOS (they use ^Z as EOF
 50173                                  ;   on devices) and programs written under the new DOS (they use the ZERO flag
 50174                                  ;   as EOF).
 50175                                  
 50176                                  ; Default SFTs for boot up
 50177                                  
 50178                                  		;PUBLIC	SFTABL
 50179                                  
 50180                                  SFTABL:	   ; LABEL   DWORD		; [SYSTEM] file table
 50181 000000CC FFFF                    		DW -1			; [SYSTEM] link to next table
 50182 000000CE FFFF                    		DW -1			; [SYSTEM] link seg to next table
 50183                                  		;dw 5 ; 24/03/2024
 50184 000000D0 0500                    		DW sf_default_number	; [SYSTEM] Number of entries in table
 50185                                  		;times 295 db 0 ; MSDOS 6.0 ; PCDOS 7.1  ; 24/03/2024
 50186 000000D2 00<rep 127h>            		times (sf_default_number*sf_entry_size) db 0
 50187                                  
 50188                                  ; the next two variables relate to the position of the logical stdout/stdin
 50189                                  ; cursor. They are only meaningful when stdin/stdout are assigned to the
 50190                                  ; console.
 50191                                  		; DOSDATA:01F9h (MSDOS 6.21) ; PCDOS 7.1 ; 24/03/2024
 50192 000001F9 00                      CARPOS:		db 0			; [SYSTEM] cursor position in stdin
 50193 000001FA 00                      STARTPOS:	db 0			; [SYSTEM] position of cursor at beginning
 50194                                  					;	   of buffered input call
 50195 000001FB 00<rep 80h>             INBUF:		times 128 db 0		; [SYSTEM] general device input buffer
 50196 0000027B 00<rep 83h>             CONBUF:		times 131 db 0		; [SYSTEM] The rest of INBUF and console buffer
 50197                                  		; DOSDATA:02FEh (MSDOS 6.21) ; PCDOS 7.1
 50198 000002FE 00                      PFLAG:		db 0			; [SYSTEM] printer echoing flag
 50199 000002FF 00                      VERFLG:		db 0			; [SYSTEM] Initialize with verify off
 50200 00000300 03                      CHARCO:		db 00000011b ; 3	; [SYSTEM] Allows statchks every 4 chars...
 50201                                  switch_character:
 50202 00000301 2F                      chSwitch:	db '/'			; UNUSED - obsolete datum, can be reused
 50203 00000302 00                      AllocMethod:	db 0			; [SYSTEM] how to alloc first(best)last
 50204 00000303 00                      fShare:		db 0			; [SYSTEM] TRUE => sharing installed
 50205 00000304 01                      DIFFNAM:	db 1			; [SYSTEM] Indicates when MYNAME has changed
 50206 00000305 20<rep 10h>             MYNAME:		times 16 db 20h		; [SYSTEM] My network name

 50421                                  ; Retro DOS v4.0 NOTE: (by Erdogan Tan, 25/04/2019)
 50422                                  ; ----------------------------------------------------------
 50423                                  ; This data section which was named as uninitialized data
 50424                                  ; (as overlayed by initialization code) but follows 
 50425                                  ; initialized data section from DOSDATA:03B6h address
 50426                                  ; (in otherwords, the method is different than MSDOS 3.3,
 50427                                  ; and there is not overlaying..)
 50428                                  ; **********************************************************
 50429                                  ; Reference: MSDOS 6.21 kernel DOSDATA section (4970 bytes)
 50430                                  ; follows DOSCODE section in the kernel file (MSDOS.SYS) 
 50431                                  ; (it is located at offset 0BF70h, file offset 0BF70h-3DE0h) 
 50432                                  ; but starts from offset 0 (ORG 0) and ends at offset 1370h.
 50433                                  ; TIMEBUF is at offset 03B6h.
 50434                                  ; **********************************************************	
 50435                                  
 50436                                  ;Break <Uninitialized data overlayed by initialization code>
 50437                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 50438                                  ;DOSDATA    SEGMENT WORD PUBLIC 'DATA'
 50439                                  ; Init code overlaps with data area below
 50440                                  
 50441                                  ; 	ORG     0
 50442                                  
 50443                                  MSDAT001S:	; label byte
 50444                                  
 50445                                  ; DOSDATA:03B6h	; MSDOS 6.21 (MSDOS.SYS, file offset 0BF70h-3DE0h+3B6h)
 50446                                  TIMEBUF: ;	times 6 db 0

 50448 000003BC 0000                    DEVIOBUF:	dw	0		; Buffer for I/O under file assignment

 51034                                  
 51035                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51036                                  ;
 51037                                  ;CASE MAPPER ROUTINE FOR 80H-FFH character range, DOS 3.3
 51038                                  ;     ENTRY: AL = Character to map
 51039                                  ;     EXIT:  AL = The converted character
 51040                                  ; Alters no registers except AL and flags.
 51041                                  ; The routine should do nothing to chars below 80H.
 51042                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51043                                  ; Example:
 51044                                  
 51045                                  MAP_CASE:
 51046                                  ;Procedure MAP_CASE,FAR
 51047                                  
 51048 00000D6B 3C80                    	CMP	AL,80h
 51049                                  	;JAE	short Map1	;Map no chars below 80H ever
 51050                                  	;RETF
 51051                                  	; 24/03/2024 (PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)
 51052                                  	;;;
 51053 00000D6D 720C                    	jb	short L_RET     ;Map no chars below 80H ever
 51054                                  	;;;
 51055                                  Map1:
 51056 00000D6F 2C80                    	SUB	AL,80h		;Turn into index value
 51057 00000D71 1E                      	PUSH	DS
 51058 00000D72 53                      	PUSH	BX
 51059 00000D73 BB[FC0A]                	MOV	BX,UCASE_TAB+2
 51060                                  FINISH:
 51061 00000D76 0E                      	PUSH	CS		;Move to DS
 51062 00000D77 1F                      	POP	DS
 51063 00000D78 D7                      	XLAT			;Get upper case character
 51064 00000D79 5B                      	POP	BX
 51065 00000D7A 1F                      	POP	DS
 51066                                  L_RET:	
 51067 00000D7B CB                      	RETF
 51068                                  
 51069                                  ;EndProc MAP_CASE

 51425                                  ;

 51428                                  ; A value of 0FFh indicates a call specific value (ie. should already
 51429                                  ; be set). AN ERROR CODE NOT IN THE TABLE FALLS THROUGH TO THE CATCH ALL AT
 51430                                  ; THE END, IT IS ASSUMES THAT CLASS, ACTION, LOCUS IS ALREADY SET.

 51438                                  ;    DB  error_&err,errCLASS_&class,errACT_&action,errLOC_&locus

 51860                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51861                                  ;
 51862                                  ; LOW MEM STUB:
 51863                                  ;
 51864                                  ; The low mem stub contains the entry points into DOS for all interrupts
 51865                                  ; handled by DOS. This stub is installed if the user specifies that the
 51866                                  ; DOS load in HIMEM. Each entry point does this.
 51867                                  ;
 51868                                  ; 	1. if jmp to 8 has been patched out
 51869                                  ;	   2. if A20 OFF
 51870                                  ;	      3. Enable A20
 51871                                  ;	   4. else 
 51872                                  ;	      5. just go to dos entry
 51873                                  ;	   6. endif
 51874                                  ;	7. else
 51875                                  ;	   8. just go to dos entry
 51876                                  ;	9. endif
 51877                                  ;
 51878                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51879                                  
 51880                                  ; 27/04/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 51881                                  
 51882                                  ; DOSDATA:108Ah (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 51883                                  
 51884                                  ; 25/03/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
 51885                                  ; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSDATA:0F9Eh
 51886                                  
 51887                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51888                                  ;
 51889                                  ; DIVIDE BY 0 handler
 51890                                  ;
 51891                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51892                                  
 51893                                  ldivov:
 51894                                  	; The following jump, skipping the XMS calls will be patched to
 51895                                  	; NOPS by SEG_REINIT if DOS successfully loads high. This jump is
 51896                                  	; needed because the stub is installed even before the XMS driver
 51897                                  	; is loaded if the user specifies dos=high in the config.sys
 51898                                  i0patch:
 51899 00000F70 EB03                    	jmp	short divov_cont
 51900                                  
 51901 00000F72 E8E200                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; we must turn on A20 if OFF
 51902                                  divov_cont:
 51903 00000F75 2EFF2E[4C0F]            	jmp	far [cs:DOSINTTABLE]	; jmp to DOS
 51904                                  
 51905                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51906                                  ;
 51907                                  ; INT 20h Handler
 51908                                  ;
 51909                                  ; Here we do not have to set up the stack to return here as the abort call
 51910                                  ; will return to the address after the int 21 ah=4b call. This would be the
 51911                                  ; common exit point if A20 had been OFF (for TOGGLE DOS) and the A20 line
 51912                                  ; will be restored then.
 51913                                  ;
 51914                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51915                                  
 51916                                  lquit:
 51917                                  	; The following jump, skipping the XMS calls will be patched to
 51918                                  	; NOPS by SEG_REINIT if DOS successfully loads high. This jump is
 51919                                  	; needed because the stub is installed even before the XMS driver
 51920                                  	; is loaded if the user specifies dos=high in the config.sys
 51921                                  i20patch:
 51922 00000F7A EB03                    	jmp	short quit_cont
 51923                                  
 51924 00000F7C E8D800                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; we must turn on A20 if OFF
 51925                                  quit_cont:
 51926 00000F7F 2EFF2E[500F]            	jmp	far [cs:DOSINTTABLE+4]	; jump to DOS
 51927                                  
 51928                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51929                                  ;
 51930                                  ; INT 21h Handler
 51931                                  ;
 51932                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
 51933                                  
 51934                                  lcommand:
 51935                                  	; The following jump, skipping the XMS calls will be patched to
 51936                                  	; NOPS by SEG_REINIT if DOS successfully loads high. This jump is
 51937                                  	; needed because the stub is installed even before the XMS driver
 51938                                  	; is loaded if the user specifies dos=high in the config.sys
 51939                                  i21patch:
 51940 00000F84 EB03                    	jmp	short command_cont
 51941                                  
 51942 00000F86 E8CE00                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; we must turn on A20 if OFF
 51943                                  command_cont:

 52046                                  
 52047                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 52048                                  ;
 52049                                  ; LowIntXX:
 52050                                  ;
 52051                                  ; Interrupts from DOS that pass control to a user program must be done from
 52052                                  ; low memory, as the user program may change the state of the A20 line or
 52053                                  ; they may require that the A20 line be OFF. The following piece of code is
 52054                                  ; far call'd from the following places in DOS:
 52055                                  ;
 52056                                  ;	1. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 23h (ctrlc)
 52057                                  ;	2. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 24h (critical error)
 52058                                  ;	3. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 28h (idle int)
 52059                                  ;
 52060                                  ; The int 23 and int 24 handlers may decide to do a far return instead of an
 52061                                  ; IRET ane leave the flags on the stack. Therefore we save the return address
 52062                                  ; before doing the ints and then do a far junp back into DOS.
 52063                                  ;
 52064                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 52065                                  
 52066                                  ; 25/03/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
 52067                                  ; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSDATA:0FEEh
 52068                                  ; (MSDOS 5.0-6.22 MSDOS.SYS - DOSDATA:10DBh)
 52069                                  
 52070 00000FC0 00000000                DosRetAddr23:	dd	0
 52071 00000FC4 00000000                DosRetAddr24:	dd	0
 52072                                  
 52073                                  ; 25/03/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
 52074                                  ; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM
 52075                                  %if 0
 52076                                  DosRetAddr28:	dd	0
 52077                                  %endif
 52078                                  
 52079                                  	; Execute int 23h from low memory
 52080                                  LowInt23:
 52081                                  					; save the return address that is on
 52082                                  					; the stack
 52083 00000FC8 2E8F06[C00F]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr23]
 52084 00000FCD 2E8F06[C20F]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr23+2]
 52085                                  
 52086 00000FD2 CD23                    	int	23h			; ctrl C
 52087                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 52088                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 52089                                  
 52090 00000FD4 E88000                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 52091                                  
 52092 00000FD7 2EFF2E[C00F]            	jmp	far [cs:DosRetAddr23]	; jump back to DOS
 52093                                  
 52094                                  
 52095                                  	; Execute int 24h from low memory
 52096                                  LowInt24:
 52097                                  					; save the return address that is on
 52098                                  					; the stack
 52099 00000FDC 2E8F06[C40F]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr24]
 52100 00000FE1 2E8F06[C60F]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr24+2]
 52101                                  
 52102 00000FE6 CD24                    	int	24h			; crit error
 52103                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 52104                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 52105                                  
 52106 00000FE8 E86C00                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 52107                                  
 52108 00000FEB 2EFF2E[C40F]            	jmp	far [cs:DosRetAddr24]	; jump back to DOS
 52109                                  
 52110                                  
 52111                                   
 52112                                  	; Execute int 28h from low memory
 52113                                  LowInt28:
 52114 00000FF0 CD28                    	int	28h			; idle int
 52115                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 52116                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 52117                                  
 52118 00000FF2 E86200                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 52119                                  
 52120 00000FF5 CB                      	retf
 52121                                  
 52122                                  ; DOSDATA:1115h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 52123                                  
 52124                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 52125                                  ;
 52126                                  ; int 21 ah=4b (exec) call will jump to the following label before xferring
 52127                                  ; control to the exec'd program. We turn off A20 inorder to allow programs
 52128                                  ; that have been packed by the faulty exepack utility to unpack correctly.
 52129                                  ; This is so because exepac'd programs rely on address wrap.
 52130                                  ;
 52131                                  ;------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 52132                                  
 52133                                  ; 25/03/2024 - Retro DOS v5.0
 52134                                  ; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSDATA:1024h
 52135                                  
 52136                                  disa20_xfer:
 52137 00000FF6 E84800                  	call	XMMDisableA20		; disable A20
 52138                                  
 52139                                  	; Look at msproc.asm at label exec_go for understanding the following:
 52140                                  
 52141                                  	; DS:SI points to entry point
 52142                                  	; AX:DI points to initial stack
 52143                                  	; DX has PDB pointer
 52144                                  	; BX has initial AX value
 52145                                  
 52146 00000FF9 FA                      	cli
 52147 00000FFA 2EC606[2103]00          	mov	byte [cs:INDOS],0	; SS Override
 52148                                  
 52149                                  	; 25/03/2024 (PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)
 52150                                  	;;;
 52151 00001000 36C606[C011]00          	mov     byte [ss:INDOS_FLAG],0
 52152                                  	;;;
 52153                                  
 52154 00001006 8ED0                    	mov	SS,AX			; set up user's stack
 52155 00001008 89FC                    	mov	SP,DI			; and SP
 52156 0000100A FB                      	sti
 52157                                  
 52158 0000100B 1E                      	push	DS			; fake long call to entry
 52159 0000100C 56                      	push	SI
 52160 0000100D 8EC2                    	mov	ES,DX			; set up proper seg registers
 52161 0000100F 8EDA                    	mov	DS,DX
 52162 00001011 89D8                    	mov	AX,BX			; set up proper AX
 52163 00001013 CB                      	retf
 52164                                  
 52165                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 52166                                  ;
 52167                                  ; M003:
 52168                                  ;
 52169                                  ; If an int 21 ah=25 call is made immediately after an exec call, DOS will
 52170                                  ; come here, turn A20 OFF restore user stack and registers before returning
 52171                                  ; to user. This is done in dos\msdisp.asm. This has been done to support 
 52172                                  ; programs compiled with MS PASCAL 3.2. See under TAG M003 in DOSSYM.INC for
 52173                                  ; more info.
 52174                                  ;
 52175                                  ; Also at this point DS is DOSDATA. So we can assume DS DOSDATA. Note that
 52176                                  ; SS is also DOS stack. It is important that we do the XMS call on DOS's
 52177                                  ; stack to avoid additional stack overhead for the user.
 52178                                  ;
 52179                                  ; -------------------------------------------------------------------------
 52180                                  
 52181                                  disa20_iret:
 52182 00001014 E82A00                  	call	XMMDisableA20
 52183 00001017 FE0E[2103]              	dec	byte [INDOS]

 52188                                  	;;;

 52193                                  	;mov	[BP+user_env.user_AX],AL
 52194 00001029 884600                  	mov	[bp],al
 52195                                  	
 52196                                  ; 25/03/2024
 52197                                  %if 0
 52198                                  	mov	AX,[NSP]
 52199                                  	mov	[USER_SP],AX
 52200                                  	mov	AX,[NSS]

 52202                                  %else

 52204                                  	;;;

 52206 0000102C C406[F005]              	les	ax,[NSS]
 52207 00001030 8C06[8405]              	mov	[USER_SP],es

 52209                                  	;;;
 52210                                  %endif

 52212 00001038 5B                      	pop	BX

 53029                                  ;============================================================================
 53030                                  ; MPATCH.ASM (MSDOS 6.0, 1993)
 53031                                  ;============================================================================
 53032                                  ; 27/04/2019 - Retro DOS 4.0
 53033                                  
 53034                                  ;mpatch.asm -- holds data patch location for callouts
 53035                                  ; -- allocate cluster in rom.asm
 53036                                  ;
 53037                                  ; This area is pointed to by OffsetMagicPatch[609h] in fixed DOS data.
 53038                                  ; Currently, this location is used only by magicdrv.sys's patch to
 53039                                  ; cluster allocation, however it can be expanded to be used by other
 53040                                  ; patches. This is important since we have an easy-access pointer to
 53041                                  ; this location in OffsetMagicPatch. Magicdrv.sys is guaranteed to
 53042                                  ; only patch out a far call/retf, so any space after that could be
 53043                                  ; used as a patch by using OffsetMagicPatch+6. See rom.asm on how
 53044                                  ; to call out here.
 53045                                  ;
 53046                                  ; Currently, we allocate only the minimum space required for the 6
 53047                                  ; byte magicdrv patch, so if you change the dos data, you may want
 53048                                  ; to reserve space here if your new data will be position dependent
 53049                                  ; and would prohibit growing of this table.
 53050                                  ;
 53051                                  ;history	-	created 8-7-92 by scottq
 53052                                  ;		-	added Rational386PatchPtr 2-1-93 by jimmat
 53053                                  ;
 53054                                  ;Exported Functions
 53055                                  ;==================
 53056                                  ;MagicPatch     -       callout patched by magidrv.sys for cluster allocations
 53057                                  
 53058                                  ; DosData Segment
 53059                                  
 53060                                  ; DOSDATA:1362h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 53061                                  
 53062                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 53063                                  
 53064                                  ; Rational386PatchPtr points to either a RET instruction (80286 or less) or
 53065                                  ; a routine to fix buggy versions of the Rational DOS Extender (80386 or
 53066                                  ; greater). Added to this file because it needed to be somewhere and is
 53067                                  ; 'patch' related.
 53068                                  
 53069                                  Rational386PatchPtr:
 53070 00001246 0000                    	dw	0	; points to patch routine or RET instr.
 53071                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 53072                                  
 53073                                  ; 25/03/2024
 53074                                  ; PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM - DOSDATA:1340h
 53075                                  ; (Windows ME IO.SYS - DOSDATA:133Eh)
 53076                                  
 53077                                  ; 07/03/2025
 53078                                  %if 0
 53079                                  MagicPatch:
 53080                                  ;MagicPatch proc far
 53081                                          retf            ;default is to just return to allocate
 53082                                          nop             ;however, this code will be patched
 53083                                          nop             ;by magicdrv.sys to
 53084                                          nop             ; call far ?:?     
 53085                                          nop             ; retf or perhaps just jmp far
 53086                                          nop             ;retf/nop take one byte, so we need six instructions
 53087                                                          ;for 6 byte patch
 53088                                  ;MagicPatch endp
 53089                                  %endif
 53090                                  
 53091                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 53092
